structure: Noun + をもって
explain: Shows the means used to do something, or the point in time when something starts or ends. It is very formal and common in announcements. It is stiffer than で or によって.

examples.jp: {本日|ほんじつ}をもって{閉店|へいてん}いたします。
examples.en: We will close our store as of today.

examples.jp: {結果|けっか}は{書面|しょめん}をもってお{知|し}らせします。
examples.en: We will inform you of the results in writing.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{誠意|せいい}をもって{謝罪|しゃざい}した。
examples.en: He apologized with sincerity.

quiz.q: {今月末|こんげつまつ}＿＿{退職|たいしょく}することになりました。
quiz.en: I will be retiring as of the end of this month.

quiz.q: {合否|ごうひ}はメール＿＿{通知|つうち}いたします。
quiz.en: We will notify you of the result by email.

quiz.q: {以上|いじょう}＿＿{本日|ほんじつ}の{会議|かいぎ}を{終|お}わります。
quiz.en: With that, we will end today's meeting.

structure: Noun + をもってしても
explain: Means "even using this strong thing, the result is still impossible." The noun is usually something powerful, like skill or money. A negative result follows. Compare をもって, which simply shows the means.

examples.jp: {最新|さいしん}の{技術|ぎじゅつ}をもってしても、この{病気|びょうき}は{治|なお}せない。
examples.en: Even with the latest technology, this illness cannot be cured.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}の{実力|じつりょく}をもってしても、{優勝|ゆうしょう}は{難|むずか}しかった。
examples.en: Even with his ability, winning was difficult.

examples.jp: どんな{言葉|ことば}をもってしても、この{感動|かんどう}は{伝|つた}えられない。
examples.en: No words can express this emotion.

quiz.q: {世界一|せかいいち}の{選手|せんしゅ}＿＿、この{記録|きろく}は{破|やぶ}れないだろう。
quiz.en: Even the world's best athlete probably could not break this record.

quiz.q: {科学|かがく}の{力|ちから}＿＿、{地震|じしん}を{正確|せいかく}に{予知|よち}することはできない。
quiz.en: Even with the power of science, earthquakes cannot be predicted accurately.

quiz.q: {大金|たいきん}＿＿、{失|うしな}った{信頼|しんらい}は{買|か}い{戻|もど}せない。
quiz.en: Even with a lot of money, you cannot buy back lost trust.

structure: Noun + を{皮切|かわき}りに
explain: Shows the first event in a series of similar events that follow. Often used for tours, sales, or a chain of events. Compare から, which only shows a starting point without the sense of "one after another."

examples.jp: {東京|とうきょう}{公演|こうえん}を{皮切|かわき}りに、{全国|ぜんこく}ツアーが{始|はじ}まった。
examples.en: Starting with the Tokyo show, the nationwide tour began.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}の{発言|はつげん}を{皮切|かわき}りに、{次々|つぎつぎ}と{反対|はんたい}{意見|いけん}が{出|で}た。
examples.en: Starting with his comment, objections came one after another.

examples.jp: この{店|みせ}は{大阪|おおさか}を{皮切|かわき}りに、{各地|かくち}に{出店|しゅってん}した。
examples.en: Starting with Osaka, this shop opened branches in many places.

quiz.q: {札幌|さっぽろ}＿＿、{全国|ぜんこく}10{都市|とし}でコンサートを{開|ひら}く。
quiz.en: Starting with Sapporo, they will hold concerts in ten cities nationwide.

quiz.q: {新製品|しんせいひん}の{発売|はつばい}＿＿、{会社|かいしゃ}の{売上|うりあげ}が{伸|の}び{始|はじ}めた。
quiz.en: Starting with the new product launch, the company's sales began to grow.

quiz.q: {一人|ひとり}の{告白|こくはく}＿＿、{多|おお}くの{被害者|ひがいしゃ}が{声|こえ}を{上|あ}げた。
quiz.en: Starting with one person's confession, many victims spoke up.

structure: Noun (time) + を{限|かぎ}りに
explain: Means something ends after this point; it is the last time. Often used with {今日|きょう}, {今回|こんかい}, or {今年|ことし}. Compare をもって, which can mark a start or an end; を{限|かぎ}りに marks only an end.

examples.jp: {今日|きょう}を{限|かぎ}りにタバコをやめます。
examples.en: As of today, I am quitting smoking.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}は{今|こん}シーズンを{限|かぎ}りに{引退|いんたい}する。
examples.en: She will retire after this season.

examples.jp: {今回|こんかい}を{限|かぎ}りに、この{大会|たいかい}は{終了|しゅうりょう}となります。
examples.en: This tournament will end after this time.

quiz.q: {今年度|こんねんど}＿＿、この{制度|せいど}は{廃止|はいし}されます。
quiz.en: This system will be abolished after this fiscal year.

quiz.q: {今夜|こんや}の{放送|ほうそう}＿＿、{番組|ばんぐみ}は{終了|しゅうりょう}します。
quiz.en: The program ends with tonight's broadcast.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{今日|きょう}＿＿{酒|さけ}を{断|た}つと{宣言|せんげん}した。
quiz.en: He declared he would give up alcohol from today.

structure: Verb (dictionary / た form) + が{早|はや}いか
explain: Something happens almost at the same moment as the first action. It describes real past events, not your own plans or commands. Similar to や{否|いな}や, but が{早|はや}いか often shows a quick, surprising action.

examples.jp: {子供|こども}は{家|いえ}に{帰|かえ}るが{早|はや}いか、{外|そと}へ{遊|あそ}びに{行|い}った。
examples.en: As soon as the child got home, he went out to play.

examples.jp: ベルが{鳴|な}るが{早|はや}いか、{学生|がくせい}たちは{教室|きょうしつ}を{飛|と}び{出|だ}した。
examples.en: The moment the bell rang, the students rushed out of the classroom.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{料理|りょうり}が{出|で}るが{早|はや}いか、{食|た}べ{始|はじ}めた。
examples.en: He started eating the moment the food came out.

quiz.q: {電車|でんしゃ}のドアが{開|ひら}く＿＿、{乗客|じょうきゃく}が{一斉|いっせい}に{降|お}りた。
quiz.en: The moment the train doors opened, the passengers all got off.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は{電話|でんわ}を{切|き}る＿＿、{家|いえ}を{出|で}た。
quiz.en: As soon as she hung up the phone, she left the house.

quiz.q: {猫|ねこ}はえさを{見|み}る＿＿、{飛|と}びついた。
quiz.en: The cat jumped on the food the moment it saw it.

structure: Verb (dictionary) + や{否|いな}や
explain: B happens right after A. It is formal and used for past facts, often in writing. Similar to が{早|はや}いか and なり; や{否|いな}や is the most written-style of the three.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{部屋|へや}に{入|はい}るや{否|いな}や、{窓|まど}を{開|あ}けた。
examples.en: The moment he entered the room, he opened the window.

examples.jp: {新商品|しんしょうひん}は{発売|はつばい}されるや{否|いな}や、{売|う}り{切|き}れた。
examples.en: The new product sold out as soon as it was released.

examples.jp: {試合|しあい}が{始|はじ}まるや{否|いな}や、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.en: No sooner had the match started than it began to rain.

quiz.q: {社長|しゃちょう}が{会場|かいじょう}に{着|つ}く＿＿、{会議|かいぎ}が{始|はじ}まった。
quiz.en: The meeting started the moment the president arrived at the venue.

quiz.q: そのニュースが{流|なが}れる＿＿、{株価|かぶか}が{急落|きゅうらく}した。
quiz.en: As soon as the news came out, the stock price fell sharply.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は{私|わたし}の{顔|かお}を{見|み}る＿＿、{泣|な}き{出|だ}した。
quiz.en: She burst into tears the moment she saw my face.

structure: Verb (dictionary) + なり
explain: Right after A, the person suddenly does B. The subject of A and B is the same, and B is often unexpected. It is more spoken than や{否|いな}や and is not used about yourself.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{帰|かえ}ってくるなり、{部屋|へや}に{閉|と}じこもった。
examples.en: As soon as he came home, he shut himself in his room.

examples.jp: {父|ちち}は{手紙|てがみ}を{読|よ}むなり、{顔色|かおいろ}を{変|か}えた。
examples.en: My father's face changed the moment he read the letter.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}は{席|せき}に{着|つ}くなり、{話|はな}し{始|はじ}めた。
examples.en: She started talking as soon as she sat down.

quiz.q: {息子|むすこ}は{家|いえ}に{帰|かえ}る＿＿、ベッドに{倒|たお}れこんだ。
quiz.en: My son collapsed onto the bed as soon as he got home.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{私|わたし}を{見|み}る＿＿、{逃|に}げ{出|だ}した。
quiz.en: He ran away the moment he saw me.

quiz.q: {部長|ぶちょう}は{会議室|かいぎしつ}に{入|はい}る＿＿、{大声|おおごえ}で{怒鳴|どな}った。
quiz.en: The manager shouted loudly as soon as he entered the meeting room.

structure: Verb (dictionary / た form) + そばから
explain: Even right after doing something, it is undone or happens again, over and over. Used for annoying repeated situations. Unlike なり, it is about a repeated pattern, not one event.

examples.jp: {片付|かたづ}けるそばから、{子供|こども}が{散|ち}らかす。
examples.en: The kids mess things up as soon as I tidy up.

examples.jp: {習|なら}ったそばから{忘|わす}れてしまう。
examples.en: I forget things right after I learn them.

examples.jp: {雪|ゆき}をかくそばから、また{積|つ}もっていく。
examples.en: As soon as I shovel the snow, it piles up again.

quiz.q: {給料|きゅうりょう}をもらう＿＿、{使|つか}ってしまう。
quiz.en: I spend my salary as soon as I get it.

quiz.q: {注意|ちゅうい}した＿＿、また{同|おな}じミスをする。
quiz.en: He makes the same mistake again right after I warn him.

quiz.q: {洗濯物|せんたくもの}を{畳|たた}む＿＿、{猫|ねこ}がその{上|うえ}で{寝|ね}る。
quiz.en: As soon as I fold the laundry, the cat sleeps on it.

structure: Verb (て form) + からというもの
explain: Since a certain event, a big change has continued until now. It is stronger than てから, and the second part describes a lasting new situation.

examples.jp: {子供|こども}が{生|う}まれてからというもの、{生活|せいかつ}が{大|おお}きく{変|か}わった。
examples.en: Ever since our child was born, our life has changed a lot.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{日本|にほん}に{来|き}てからというもの、{毎日|まいにち}{日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}している。
examples.en: Ever since he came to Japan, he has studied Japanese every day.

examples.jp: {犬|いぬ}を{飼|か}い{始|はじ}めてからというもの、{毎朝|まいあさ}{散歩|さんぽ}している。
examples.en: Ever since I started keeping a dog, I go for a walk every morning.

quiz.q: {禁煙|きんえん}して＿＿、{体|からだ}の{調子|ちょうし}がとてもいい。
quiz.en: Ever since I quit smoking, I have felt very healthy.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}と{別|わか}れて＿＿、{彼|かれ}は{元気|げんき}がない。
quiz.en: Ever since he broke up with her, he has been down.

quiz.q: スマホを{買|か}って＿＿、{本|ほん}を{読|よ}まなくなった。
quiz.en: Ever since I bought a smartphone, I stopped reading books.

structure: Verb (た form) + が{最後|さいご}
explain: Once something happens, a bad result surely follows and cannot be stopped. たら{最後|さいご} is the casual version. It always leads to a negative or unstoppable result.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{寝|ね}たが{最後|さいご}、{何|なに}があっても{起|お}きない。
examples.en: Once he falls asleep, nothing will wake him.

examples.jp: このお{菓子|かし}は{食|た}べ{始|はじ}めたが{最後|さいご}、{止|と}まらなくなる。
examples.en: Once you start eating these sweets, you can't stop.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}に{秘密|ひみつ}を{話|はな}したら{最後|さいご}、みんなに{広|ひろ}まってしまう。
examples.en: Once you tell her a secret, everyone will hear it.

quiz.q: あの{人|ひと}にお{金|かね}を{貸|か}した＿＿、{二度|にど}と{返|かえ}ってこない。
quiz.en: Once you lend that person money, you'll never get it back.

quiz.q: {父|ちち}は{怒|おこ}り{出|だ}した＿＿、{誰|だれ}にも{止|と}められない。
quiz.en: Once my father starts getting angry, no one can stop him.

quiz.q: このゲームは{一度|いちど}{始|はじ}めた＿＿、{朝|あさ}までやめられない。
quiz.en: Once you start this game, you can't stop until morning.

structure: Noun + をおいて（ほかに）～ない
explain: Means "there is no one or nothing else besides this." It is used to praise someone or something as the only choice. The sentence ends in a negative like いない or ない.

examples.jp: この{仕事|しごと}を{任|まか}せられるのは、{彼|かれ}をおいてほかにいない。
examples.en: There is no one but him we can trust with this job.

examples.jp: {桜|さくら}を{見|み}るなら、{京都|きょうと}をおいてほかにない。
examples.en: If you want to see cherry blossoms, there is no place like Kyoto.

examples.jp: {今|いま}をおいて、チャンスはない。
examples.en: There is no chance other than now.

quiz.q: {次|つぎ}のリーダーにふさわしいのは、{田中|たなか}さん＿＿ほかにいない。
quiz.en: There is no one more suitable as the next leader than Mr. Tanaka.

quiz.q: この{問題|もんだい}を{解決|かいけつ}できるのは、あなた＿＿いません。
quiz.en: No one but you can solve this problem.

quiz.q: {留学|りゅうがく}するなら、{今|いま}＿＿ない。
quiz.en: If you are going to study abroad, now is the only time.

structure: Noun + ならでは（の）
explain: Shows something that only this person, place, or thing can have or do. It is used to praise. It is often used as ならではの + noun.

examples.jp: これは{京都|きょうと}ならではの{景色|けしき}です。
examples.en: This is a view you can only see in Kyoto.

examples.jp: {子供|こども}ならではの{自由|じゆう}な{発想|はっそう}に{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.en: I was surprised by the free ideas that only a child could have.

examples.jp: この{味|あじ}は{老舗|しにせ}ならではだ。
examples.en: Only a long-established shop can make this taste.

quiz.q: {手作|てづく}り＿＿の{温|あたた}かさがある。
quiz.en: It has a warmth that only handmade things have.

quiz.q: {北海道|ほっかいどう}＿＿の{新鮮|しんせん}な{海産物|かいさんぶつ}を{楽|たの}しんだ。
quiz.en: We enjoyed fresh seafood that you can only get in Hokkaido.

quiz.q: これはプロ＿＿の{技術|ぎじゅつ}だ。
quiz.en: This is a skill that only a professional has.

structure: Noun / Verb (plain) + にとどまらず
explain: Something goes beyond a certain range and spreads wider. It is similar to だけでなく, but it stresses that the range is wider than expected.

examples.jp: その{影響|えいきょう}は{国内|こくない}にとどまらず、{海外|かいがい}にも{広|ひろ}がった。
examples.en: The influence was not limited to Japan; it spread overseas too.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}の{活動|かつどう}は{音楽|おんがく}にとどまらず、{映画|えいが}にも{及|およ}ぶ。
examples.en: His work is not limited to music; it extends to film too.

examples.jp: この{問題|もんだい}は{一|ひと}つの{町|まち}にとどまらず、{県|けん}{全体|ぜんたい}の{問題|もんだい}だ。
examples.en: This problem is not just one town's; it concerns the whole prefecture.

quiz.q: {被害|ひがい}は{東京|とうきょう}＿＿、{関東|かんとう}{全域|ぜんいき}に{及|およ}んだ。
quiz.en: The damage was not limited to Tokyo; it reached the whole Kanto region.

quiz.q: そのアプリは{若者|わかもの}＿＿、{高齢者|こうれいしゃ}にも{人気|にんき}だ。
quiz.en: The app is popular not only with young people but also with elderly people.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}の{研究|けんきゅう}は{日本|にほん}＿＿、{世界|せかい}で{評価|ひょうか}されている。
quiz.en: His research is valued not only in Japan but around the world.

structure: Noun + はおろか
explain: Means "A, of course, and even B (a more extreme case)." It is usually followed by も or さえ and has a negative feeling. Compare どころか, which can also mean "far from"; はおろか cannot.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{漢字|かんじ}はおろか、ひらがなも{読|よ}めない。
examples.en: He can't read hiragana, let alone kanji.

examples.jp: {忙|いそが}しくて、{旅行|りょこう}はおろか{休日|きゅうじつ}もない。
examples.en: I'm so busy I don't even have days off, let alone trips.

examples.jp: {事故|じこ}で{歩|ある}くことはおろか、{立|た}つこともできなくなった。
examples.en: After the accident, I couldn't even stand, let alone walk.

quiz.q: {車|くるま}＿＿、{自転車|じてんしゃ}さえ{持|も}っていない。
quiz.en: I don't even have a bicycle, let alone a car.

quiz.q: {英語|えいご}＿＿、{日本語|にほんご}もうまく{話|はな}せない。
quiz.en: He can't even speak Japanese well, let alone English.

quiz.q: {貯金|ちょきん}＿＿、{明日|あした}の{食費|しょくひ}もない。
quiz.en: I don't even have money for tomorrow's food, let alone savings.

structure: Noun + もさることながら
explain: A is of course good, but B is even more important or notable. It is used for positive points. Compare はおろか, which is used for negative situations.

examples.jp: この{店|みせ}は{味|あじ}もさることながら、{雰囲気|ふんいき}もすばらしい。
examples.en: This restaurant's food is good, and the atmosphere is wonderful too.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{成績|せいせき}もさることながら、{人柄|ひとがら}もいい。
examples.en: His grades are good, and his character is good too.

examples.jp: {本人|ほんにん}の{努力|どりょく}もさることながら、{家族|かぞく}の{支|ささ}えも{大|おお}きかった。
examples.en: His own effort mattered, but his family's support was also big.

quiz.q: このホテルは{景色|けしき}＿＿、サービスも{一流|いちりゅう}だ。
quiz.en: This hotel's view is great, and its service is also first-class.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}の{歌|うた}は{声|こえ}＿＿、{表現力|ひょうげんりょく}が{素晴|すば}らしい。
quiz.en: Her voice is lovely, but her expressiveness is even more wonderful.

quiz.q: デザイン＿＿、{使|つか}いやすさが{評価|ひょうか}されている。
quiz.en: Its design is good, but its ease of use is praised even more.

structure: ただ + Noun / Verb (dictionary) + のみ
explain: A formal way to say "only." It is stronger and more written than だけ. ただ～のみならず means "not only."

examples.jp: {今|いま}はただ{結果|けっか}を{待|ま}つのみだ。
examples.en: Now all we can do is wait for the result.

examples.jp: {私|わたし}に{必要|ひつよう}なのは、ただ{時間|じかん}のみです。
examples.en: All I need is time.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}はただ{黙|だま}って{聞|き}くのみだった。
examples.en: He only listened in silence.

quiz.q: {準備|じゅんび}は{終|お}わった。あとはただ{本番|ほんばん}を{迎|むか}える＿＿だ。
quiz.en: The preparation is done. All that's left is to face the real thing.

quiz.q: {合格|ごうかく}できたのは、ただ{努力|どりょく}＿＿によるものだ。
quiz.en: I passed only because of hard work.

quiz.q: {被災地|ひさいち}の{一日|いちにち}も{早|はや}い{復興|ふっこう}を、ただ{祈|いの}る＿＿です。
quiz.en: We can only pray for the quick recovery of the disaster area.

structure: {一|いち} + Counter + たりとも～ない
explain: Means "not even one," used with the smallest amount, like {一日|いちにち} or {一円|いちえん}. It is always followed by a negative. It is stronger than も.

examples.jp: {一日|いちにち}たりとも{練習|れんしゅう}を{休|やす}んだことはない。
examples.en: I have never missed practice, not even for a single day.

examples.jp: {一円|いちえん}たりとも{無駄|むだ}にはできない。
examples.en: I can't waste even a single yen.

examples.jp: {試験|しけん}まで{一分|いっぷん}たりとも{無駄|むだ}にできない。
examples.en: I can't waste even a minute before the exam.

quiz.q: {一瞬|いっしゅん}＿＿{油断|ゆだん}してはいけない。
quiz.en: You must not let your guard down even for a moment.

quiz.q: {一人|ひとり}＿＿{見逃|みのが}さない。
quiz.en: We won't let even one person get away.

quiz.q: この{仕事|しごと}では、{一度|いちど}＿＿ミスは{許|ゆる}されない。
quiz.en: In this job, not even a single mistake is allowed.

structure: Noun (+ particle) + すら
explain: Means "even," showing an extreme example. It is like さえ but more written. It is often used with negatives.

examples.jp: {疲|つか}れて{歩|ある}くことすらできない。
examples.en: I'm so tired I can't even walk.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{自分|じぶん}の{名前|なまえ}すら{書|か}けない。
examples.en: He can't even write his own name.

examples.jp: そんなことは{子供|こども}ですら{知|し}っている。
examples.en: Even a child knows that.

quiz.q: {忙|いそが}しくて、{寝|ね}る{時間|じかん}＿＿ない。
quiz.en: I'm so busy that I don't even have time to sleep.

quiz.q: {専門家|せんもんか}＿＿{分|わ}からない{問題|もんだい}だ。
quiz.en: It is a problem that even experts don't understand.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{挨拶|あいさつ}＿＿しないで{帰|かえ}った。
quiz.en: He went home without even saying hello.

structure: Verb (dictionary) / Noun + だに
explain: Means "even just" doing something like thinking or imagining. It is used with a few words: {想像|そうぞう}するだに, {考|かんが}えるだに, {夢|ゆめ}にだに, {微動|びどう}だにしない. It is very literary.

examples.jp: {事故|じこ}のことは、{思|おも}い{出|だ}すだに{恐|おそ}ろしい。
examples.en: Just remembering the accident is frightening.

examples.jp: {優勝|ゆうしょう}するなんて、{夢|ゆめ}にだに{思|おも}わなかった。
examples.en: I never even dreamed of winning.

examples.jp: {兵士|へいし}たちは{微動|びどう}だにしなかった。
examples.en: The soldiers did not move at all.

quiz.q: {地震|じしん}が{来|き}たらと{想像|そうぞう}する＿＿{恐|おそ}ろしい。
quiz.en: Just imagining an earthquake hitting is frightening.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{何|なに}を{言|い}われても{微動|びどう}＿＿しなかった。
quiz.en: He didn't move at all, no matter what was said to him.

quiz.q: {戦争|せんそう}のことは、{考|かんが}える＿＿{胸|むね}が{痛|いた}む。
quiz.en: Just thinking about war makes my heart ache.

structure: Number + Counter + からある / からする / からの
explain: Stresses a large size, weight, or amount: "as much as" or "more than." からする is for prices, からある is for size or weight, and からの is used before a noun for people or things.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は100キロからある{荷物|にもつ}を{一人|ひとり}で{運|はこ}んだ。
examples.en: He carried a load of over 100 kilograms by himself.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}は100{万円|まんえん}からするバッグを{買|か}った。
examples.en: She bought a bag that costs a million yen or more.

examples.jp: {会場|かいじょう}には1{万人|まんにん}からの{観客|かんきゃく}が{集|あつ}まった。
examples.en: As many as ten thousand spectators gathered at the venue.

quiz.q: 3メートル＿＿{大|おお}きな{魚|さかな}が{釣|つ}れた。
quiz.en: We caught a huge fish of three meters or more.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は1{本|ぽん}10{万円|まんえん}＿＿ワインを{開|あ}けた。
quiz.en: He opened a bottle of wine that costs 100,000 yen or more.

quiz.q: {駅前|えきまえ}には5{千人|せんにん}＿＿{人々|ひとびと}が{集|あつ}まった。
quiz.en: As many as 5,000 people gathered in front of the station.

structure: Noun + にあって
explain: Means "in this special situation or position." It is formal and stresses that the situation matters. Compare において, which simply marks a place or time.

examples.jp: {不況|ふきょう}にあって、この{会社|かいしゃ}は{成長|せいちょう}を{続|つづ}けている。
examples.en: Even in a recession, this company keeps growing.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{社長|しゃちょう}という{立場|たちば}にあって、{責任|せきにん}を{感|かん}じている。
examples.en: In his position as president, he feels responsible.

examples.jp: {極限|きょくげん}{状態|じょうたい}にあって、{人|ひと}は{本当|ほんとう}の{姿|すがた}を{見|み}せる。
examples.en: In extreme situations, people show their true selves.

quiz.q: {物|もの}が{豊|ゆた}かな{現代|げんだい}＿＿、{物|もの}を{大切|たいせつ}にする{心|こころ}が{失|うしな}われつつある。
quiz.en: In modern times, when things are plentiful, the habit of caring for things is being lost.

quiz.q: {非常時|ひじょうじ}＿＿、{冷静|れいせい}な{判断|はんだん}が{求|もと}められる。
quiz.en: In an emergency, calm judgment is needed.

quiz.q: {指導者|しどうしゃ}の{地位|ちい}＿＿、{軽率|けいそつ}な{発言|はつげん}は{許|ゆる}されない。
quiz.en: In a leader's position, careless comments are not allowed.

structure: Noun / Verb (dictionary) + に{至|いた}って（は）
explain: に{至|いた}って means "only after things reached this (bad) point." に{至|いた}っては picks the most extreme example in a list. Both are formal.

examples.jp: {事故|じこ}が{起|お}きるに{至|いた}って、{初|はじ}めて{安全|あんぜん}{対策|たいさく}が{取|と}られた。
examples.en: Only when an accident happened were safety measures taken.

examples.jp: {家族|かぞく}みんな{料理|りょうり}が{苦手|にがて}だが、{父|ちち}に{至|いた}っては{卵|たまご}も{焼|や}けない。
examples.en: My whole family is bad at cooking; as for my father, he can't even fry an egg.

examples.jp: {倒産|とうさん}するに{至|いた}って、{社長|しゃちょう}はやっと{失敗|しっぱい}を{認|みと}めた。
examples.en: Only when the company went bankrupt did the president admit his failure.

quiz.q: {病気|びょうき}が{悪化|あっか}する＿＿、{彼|かれ}はようやく{病院|びょういん}に{行|い}った。
quiz.en: Only when his illness got worse did he finally go to the hospital.

quiz.q: クラスの{誰|だれ}も{宿題|しゅくだい}をしていない。{田中君|たなかくん}＿＿、{教科書|きょうかしょ}も{持|も}ってきていない。
quiz.en: Nobody in class did the homework. As for Tanaka, he didn't even bring his textbook.

quiz.q: {問題|もんだい}が{国会|こっかい}で{取|と}り{上|あ}げられる＿＿、{国民|こくみん}は{事|こと}の{重大|じゅうだい}さを{知|し}った。
quiz.en: Only when the issue was raised in the Diet did the public realize how serious it was.

structure: Noun + に{至|いた}るまで
explain: Shows that a range goes all the way to a surprising or small detail. It is stronger than まで and is often used with から: AからBに{至|いた}るまで.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{服|ふく}から{靴下|くつした}に{至|いた}るまで、ブランド{品|ひん}だ。
examples.en: From his clothes down to his socks, everything is brand-name.

examples.jp: この{店|みせ}は{食器|しょっき}からスプーンに{至|いた}るまで{手作|てづく}りだ。
examples.en: In this shop, everything from the dishes down to the spoons is handmade.

examples.jp: {規則|きそく}は{髪型|かみがた}に{至|いた}るまで{細|こま}かく{決|き}められている。
examples.en: The rules are set in detail, even down to hairstyles.

quiz.q: {子供|こども}からお{年寄|としよ}り＿＿、{誰|だれ}でも{楽|たの}しめるイベントだ。
quiz.en: It is an event anyone can enjoy, from children to the elderly.

quiz.q: {警察|けいさつ}は{部屋|へや}の{隅々|すみずみ}＿＿{調|しら}べた。
quiz.en: The police searched even every corner of the room.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は{言葉遣|ことばづか}いから{歩|ある}き{方|かた}＿＿、{母親|ははおや}にそっくりだ。
quiz.en: From the way she talks down to the way she walks, she is just like her mother.

structure: Noun + を{経|へ}て
explain: Shows a process, place, or time that you pass through to reach a result. It is formal. Compare を{通|つう}じて, which means "through" as a channel or over a period.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{厳|きび}しい{修行|しゅぎょう}を{経|へ}て、{一流|いちりゅう}のシェフになった。
examples.en: After hard training, he became a top chef.

examples.jp: {飛行機|ひこうき}はソウルを{経|へ}て、{東京|とうきょう}に{着|つ}いた。
examples.en: The plane arrived in Tokyo via Seoul.

examples.jp: {長|なが}い{話|はな}し{合|あ}いを{経|へ}て、{計画|けいかく}が{決|き}まった。
examples.en: After long discussions, the plan was decided.

quiz.q: {十年|じゅうねん}の{歳月|さいげつ}＿＿、{橋|はし}が{完成|かんせい}した。
quiz.en: After ten years, the bridge was completed.

quiz.q: {予選|よせん}＿＿、{決勝|けっしょう}に{進|すす}んだ。
quiz.en: After the preliminary round, they moved on to the finals.

quiz.q: {多|おお}くの{失敗|しっぱい}＿＿、{新|あたら}しい{薬|くすり}が{生|う}まれた。
quiz.en: After many failures, a new medicine was created.

structure: Noun + をよそに
explain: Someone acts without caring about other people's worry, opinions, or expectations. It often has a slightly critical feeling. Compare をものともせず, which praises courage against difficulty.

examples.jp: {親|おや}の{心配|しんぱい}をよそに、{彼|かれ}は{一人|ひとり}で{旅|たび}に{出|で}た。
examples.en: Ignoring his parents' worries, he set off on a trip alone.

examples.jp: {住民|じゅうみん}の{反対|はんたい}をよそに、{工事|こうじ}が{始|はじ}まった。
examples.en: Construction started despite the residents' opposition.

examples.jp: {周|まわ}りの{期待|きたい}をよそに、{彼女|かのじょ}は{試合|しあい}に{負|ま}けた。
examples.en: Contrary to everyone's hopes, she lost the match.

quiz.q: {医者|いしゃ}の{注意|ちゅうい}＿＿、{父|ちち}はまたお{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}んでいる。
quiz.en: Ignoring the doctor's warning, my father is drinking again.

quiz.q: {家族|かぞく}の{心配|しんぱい}＿＿、{弟|おとうと}は{毎晩|まいばん}{遅|おそ}くまで{遊|あそ}んでいる。
quiz.en: Ignoring the family's worries, my younger brother goes out late every night.

quiz.q: {国民|こくみん}の{不安|ふあん}＿＿、{政府|せいふ}は{増税|ぞうぜい}を{決|き}めた。
quiz.en: Ignoring the public's concerns, the government decided to raise taxes.

meaning: in defiance of ~ / not letting ~ stop them
structure: Noun + をものともせず（に）
explain: Someone bravely overcomes a hardship and does not let it stop them. It is used to praise others, not yourself. Compare をよそに, which shows ignoring other people's feelings.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{足|あし}のけがをものともせず、{最後|さいご}まで{走|はし}った。
examples.en: Not letting his leg injury stop him, he ran to the end.

examples.jp: {選手|せんしゅ}たちは{大雨|おおあめ}をものともせずに{試合|しあい}を{続|つづ}けた。
examples.en: The players kept playing despite the heavy rain.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}は{周囲|しゅうい}の{批判|ひはん}をものともせず、{夢|ゆめ}を{追|お}い{続|つづ}けた。
examples.en: Undaunted by criticism, she kept chasing her dream.

quiz.q: {登山隊|とざんたい}は{吹雪|ふぶき}＿＿、{頂上|ちょうじょう}を{目指|めざ}した。
quiz.en: The climbing team aimed for the summit in spite of the blizzard.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{貧|まず}しさ＿＿、{医者|いしゃ}になる{夢|ゆめ}をかなえた。
quiz.en: Undaunted by poverty, he achieved his dream of becoming a doctor.

quiz.q: {救助隊|きゅうじょたい}は{危険|きけん}＿＿、{人々|ひとびと}を{助|たす}けに{向|む}かった。
quiz.en: The rescue team went to help people, undeterred by the danger.

structure: Noun / plain form + のをいいことに
explain: Someone uses a situation for a selfish or bad purpose. It has a critical feeling. Compare をきっかけに, which is neutral.

examples.jp: {親|おや}が{留守|るす}なのをいいことに、{子供|こども}たちは{夜|よる}{遅|おそ}くまでゲームをした。
examples.en: Taking advantage of their parents being away, the kids played games until late.

examples.jp: {先生|せんせい}が{優|やさ}しいのをいいことに、{彼|かれ}は{宿題|しゅくだい}をしない。
examples.en: Taking advantage of the teacher being kind, he doesn't do his homework.

examples.jp: {誰|だれ}も{見|み}ていないのをいいことに、{彼|かれ}はごみを{捨|す}てた。
examples.en: Taking advantage of nobody watching, he threw away his trash.

quiz.q: {上司|じょうし}がいないの＿＿、{彼|かれ}は{仕事中|しごとちゅう}に{寝|ね}ていた。
quiz.en: Taking advantage of the boss's absence, he slept during work.

quiz.q: {文句|もんく}を{言|い}われないの＿＿、{隣人|りんじん}は{毎晩|まいばん}{騒|さわ}いでいる。
quiz.en: Taking advantage of no one complaining, my neighbor makes noise every night.

quiz.q: {規則|きそく}があいまいなの＿＿、{勝手|かって}なことをする{人|ひと}がいる。
quiz.en: Some people take advantage of the vague rules to do as they please.

structure: Noun + に{即|そく}して / に{即|そく}した + Noun
explain: Means acting in a way that fits facts, rules, or reality. It is formal. Compare にそって, which means following a plan or guideline.

examples.jp: {事実|じじつ}に{即|そく}して{報告|ほうこく}してください。
examples.en: Please report based on the facts.

examples.jp: {法律|ほうりつ}に{即|そく}して{判断|はんだん}する。
examples.en: We will judge according to the law.

examples.jp: {現実|げんじつ}に{即|そく}した{計画|けいかく}を{立|た}てるべきだ。
examples.en: We should make a plan that fits reality.

quiz.q: {時代|じだい}の{変化|へんか}＿＿、{制度|せいど}を{見直|みなお}す{必要|ひつよう}がある。
quiz.en: We need to review the system in line with the changing times.

quiz.q: {学生|がくせい}の{実態|じったい}＿＿{指導|しどう}を{行|おこな}う。
quiz.en: We give guidance based on the students' actual situation.

quiz.q: {規則|きそく}＿＿{処理|しょり}しますので、{例外|れいがい}は{認|みと}められません。
quiz.en: We will handle it according to the rules, so no exceptions are allowed.

structure: Noun + にかかわる
explain: Means something seriously affects an important thing, like life, honor, or the future. It is used for big, serious matters, not small ones.

examples.jp: これは{命|いのち}にかかわる{問題|もんだい}だ。
examples.en: This is a matter of life and death.

examples.jp: {会社|かいしゃ}の{信用|しんよう}にかかわるので、ミスは{許|ゆる}されない。
examples.en: It affects the company's reputation, so mistakes are not allowed.

examples.jp: {将来|しょうらい}にかかわる{大事|だいじ}な{決断|けつだん}をした。
examples.en: I made an important decision that affects my future.

quiz.q: そんなことをしたら、{君|きみ}の{名誉|めいよ}＿＿よ。
quiz.en: If you do that, it will affect your honor.

quiz.q: {小|ちい}さなけがでも、{放|ほう}っておくと{命|いのち}＿＿ことがある。
quiz.en: Even a small injury can become life-threatening if left alone.

quiz.q: {環境|かんきょう}{問題|もんだい}は、{人類|じんるい}の{未来|みらい}＿＿{重要|じゅうよう}な{課題|かだい}だ。
quiz.en: Environmental problems are an important issue that affects humanity's future.

structure: Noun / plain form + の + にひきかえ
explain: Compares two things that are very different, often with the speaker's feeling (praise or criticism). It is more emotional than に{比|くら}べて or に{対|たい}して.

examples.jp: {兄|あに}にひきかえ、{弟|おとうと}はよく{勉強|べんきょう}する。
examples.en: In contrast to his older brother, the younger brother studies hard.

examples.jp: {去年|きょねん}の{暑|あつ}さにひきかえ、{今年|ことし}の{夏|なつ}は{涼|すず}しい。
examples.en: Unlike last year's heat, this summer is cool.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}が{真面目|まじめ}なのにひきかえ、{私|わたし}は{怠|なま}け{者|もの}だ。
examples.en: While he is serious, I am lazy.

quiz.q: {明|あか}るい{姉|あね}＿＿、{妹|いもうと}はとてもおとなしい。
quiz.en: Unlike her cheerful older sister, the younger sister is very quiet.

quiz.q: {前|まえ}の{部長|ぶちょう}が{厳|きび}しかったの＿＿、{今|いま}の{部長|ぶちょう}はとても{優|やさ}しい。
quiz.en: While the previous manager was strict, the current one is very kind.

quiz.q: {都会|とかい}の{忙|いそが}しさ＿＿、この{村|むら}は{時間|じかん}がゆっくり{流|なが}れている。
quiz.en: Unlike the busy city, time passes slowly in this village.

structure: Noun / Question word + にもまして
explain: Means "even more than (something that was already high)." With question words, like {何|なに}にもまして, it means "more than anything." Compare より, which is a simple comparison.

examples.jp: {今年|ことし}の{夏|なつ}は{去年|きょねん}にもまして{暑|あつ}い。
examples.en: This summer is even hotter than last year.

examples.jp: {何|なに}にもまして{健康|けんこう}が{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.en: Health is more important than anything.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}は{以前|いぜん}にもまして{美|うつく}しくなった。
examples.en: She has become even more beautiful than before.

quiz.q: {今日|きょう}の{試験|しけん}は{前回|ぜんかい}＿＿{難|むずか}しかった。
quiz.en: Today's exam was even harder than the last one.

quiz.q: {誰|だれ}＿＿{努力|どりょく}したのは{彼|かれ}だ。
quiz.en: He is the one who worked harder than anyone.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}の{病状|びょうじょう}は{昨日|きのう}＿＿{悪|わる}くなっている。
quiz.en: His condition is even worse than yesterday.

structure: Noun + ときたら
explain: Used to bring up a person or thing and complain about them. It is casual and shows the speaker's frustration. Compare といえば, which is neutral.

examples.jp: うちの{息子|むすこ}ときたら、{毎日|まいにち}ゲームばかりしている。
examples.en: My son is always playing games every day.

examples.jp: この{店|みせ}のサービスときたら、{本当|ほんとう}にひどい。
examples.en: As for this shop's service, it's really terrible.

examples.jp: {最近|さいきん}の{天気|てんき}ときたら、{雨|あめ}ばかりで{嫌|いや}になる。
examples.en: The weather lately is all rain, it's depressing.

quiz.q: うちの{夫|おっと}＿＿、{家事|かじ}を{全然|ぜんぜん}{手伝|てつだ}わない。
quiz.en: My husband never helps with the housework at all.

quiz.q: このパソコン＿＿、すぐに{止|と}まってしまう。
quiz.en: This computer keeps freezing all the time.

quiz.q: {隣|となり}の{犬|いぬ}＿＿、{一日中|いちにちじゅう}{吠|ほ}えてうるさい。
quiz.en: The neighbor's dog barks all day, it's so noisy.

meaning: when it comes to (a higher level) ~
structure: Noun / Verb (dictionary) + ともなると / ともなれば
explain: When something reaches a higher level or special position, things naturally change. Often used with age, rank, or seasons. It is stronger than になると.

examples.jp: {大学生|だいがくせい}ともなると、{自分|じぶん}で{考|かんが}えて{行動|こうどう}しなければならない。
examples.en: Once you become a university student, you must think and act for yourself.

examples.jp: {社長|しゃちょう}ともなると、{休|やす}む{暇|ひま}もないだろう。
examples.en: When you become company president, you probably don't even have time to rest.

examples.jp: {年末|ねんまつ}ともなると、{街|まち}はにぎやかになる。
examples.en: At the end of the year, the town becomes lively.

quiz.q: プロ＿＿、{練習|れんしゅう}の{量|りょう}も{違|ちが}う。
quiz.en: When you are a professional, the amount of practice is different too.

quiz.q: {結婚|けっこん}する＿＿、いろいろ{準備|じゅんび}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
quiz.en: When it comes to getting married, you need many preparations.

quiz.q: {十二月|じゅうにがつ}＿＿、{朝晩|あさばん}はかなり{冷|ひ}える。
quiz.en: When it gets to December, mornings and evenings get quite cold.

structure: ともあろう + Noun (person/organization)
explain: Means "someone of such a high position" did something they shouldn't. It expresses surprise or criticism. It is followed by a word for a person or group.

examples.jp: {教師|きょうし}ともあろう{者|もの}が、{生徒|せいと}にうそをつくなんて。
examples.en: How could a teacher, of all people, lie to students?

examples.jp: {大臣|だいじん}ともあろう{人|ひと}が、そんな{発言|はつげん}をするとは。
examples.en: I can't believe a minister would say such a thing.

examples.jp: {一流|いちりゅう}{企業|きぎょう}ともあろう{会社|かいしゃ}が、データを{偽|いつわ}っていた。
examples.en: A top company, of all things, was faking data.

quiz.q: {警察官|けいさつかん}＿＿{者|もの}が、{法律|ほうりつ}を{破|やぶ}るとは{何事|なにごと}だ。
quiz.en: How dare a police officer break the law!

quiz.q: {医者|いしゃ}＿＿{人|ひと}が、こんな{簡単|かんたん}なミスをするなんて。
quiz.en: I can't believe a doctor would make such a simple mistake.

quiz.q: {横綱|よこづな}＿＿{者|もの}が、{負|ま}けて{言|い}い{訳|わけ}をするべきではない。
quiz.en: A grand champion shouldn't make excuses after losing.

structure: Noun + たる + Noun（{者|もの}）
explain: Means "being someone in this role, you should act properly." It is very formal and often followed by べきだ or なければならない. Compare として, which is neutral.

examples.jp: {教師|きょうし}たる{者|もの}、{生徒|せいと}の{手本|てほん}にならなければならない。
examples.en: A teacher must be a model for the students.

examples.jp: {政治家|せいじか}たる{者|もの}は{国民|こくみん}のために{働|はたら}くべきだ。
examples.en: A politician should work for the people.

examples.jp: {王|おう}たる{者|もの}、{民|たみ}を{守|まも}るべきだ。
examples.en: One who is king must protect the people.

quiz.q: {医者|いしゃ}＿＿{者|もの}、{患者|かんじゃ}の{命|いのち}を{第一|だいいち}に{考|かんが}えるべきだ。
quiz.en: A doctor should put the patient's life first.

quiz.q: {社会人|しゃかいじん}＿＿もの、{時間|じかん}は{守|まも}らなければならない。
quiz.en: A working adult must be on time.

quiz.q: {親|おや}＿＿{者|もの}、{子供|こども}の{安全|あんぜん}を{守|まも}る{責任|せきにん}がある。
quiz.en: Parents have a responsibility to keep their children safe.

structure: Noun / plain form + とあって
explain: Gives a special reason, and the result is natural for that situation. It is often used in news. Compare ので, which is a general reason.

examples.jp: {連休|れんきゅう}とあって、{観光地|かんこうち}はどこも{混|こ}んでいる。
examples.en: Because it's a long holiday, every tourist spot is crowded.

examples.jp: {人気|にんき}{歌手|かしゅ}が{来|く}るとあって、{会場|かいじょう}は{満員|まんいん}だ。
examples.en: Because a popular singer is coming, the venue is full.

examples.jp: {初|はじ}めての{海外|かいがい}{旅行|りょこう}とあって、{娘|むすめ}はわくわくしている。
examples.en: Because it is her first trip abroad, my daughter is excited.

quiz.q: {年|とし}に{一度|いちど}の{祭|まつ}り＿＿、{町|まち}はたくさんの{人|ひと}でにぎわった。
quiz.en: Because it was the once-a-year festival, the town was crowded with people.

quiz.q: {無料|むりょう}＿＿、{店|みせ}の{前|まえ}には{長|なが}い{列|れつ}ができた。
quiz.en: Because it was free, a long line formed in front of the shop.

quiz.q: {週末|しゅうまつ}＿＿、{遊園地|ゆうえんち}は{家族連|かぞくづ}れでいっぱいだ。
quiz.en: Because it's the weekend, the amusement park is full of families.

meaning: if it is for ~ (I will do it)
structure: Noun / plain form + とあれば
explain: Means "if it is for this reason, I am willing to do even hard things." It shows strong will. Compare なら, which is a simple condition.

examples.jp: {子供|こども}のためとあれば、どんな{苦労|くろう}もいとわない。
examples.en: If it's for my children, I'll endure any hardship.

examples.jp: {社長|しゃちょう}の{命令|めいれい}とあれば、{従|したが}うしかない。
examples.en: If it's the president's order, we have no choice but to follow.

examples.jp: {必要|ひつよう}とあれば、いつでも{駆|か}けつけます。
examples.en: If needed, I'll come running anytime.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}に{会|あ}える＿＿、どこへでも{行|い}く。
quiz.en: If I can meet her, I'll go anywhere.

quiz.q: お{客様|きゃくさま}の{頼|たの}み＿＿、{断|ことわ}るわけにはいかない。
quiz.en: If it's a customer's request, we can't refuse.

quiz.q: {家族|かぞく}を{守|まも}るため＿＿、{私|わたし}は{何|なん}でもする。
quiz.en: If it's to protect my family, I'll do anything.

structure: Noun / plain form + といえども
explain: Means "even though it is A (which you might expect otherwise), still B." It is formal. Compare とはいえ, which is closer to "that said."

examples.jp: {子供|こども}といえども、ルールは{守|まも}らなければならない。
examples.en: Even a child must follow the rules.

examples.jp: {専門家|せんもんか}といえども、{間違|まちが}えることはある。
examples.en: Even experts make mistakes sometimes.

examples.jp: {休日|きゅうじつ}といえども、{社長|しゃちょう}は{休|やす}めない。
examples.en: Even on holidays, the president can't rest.

quiz.q: {大統領|だいとうりょう}＿＿、{法律|ほうりつ}に{従|したが}わなければならない。
quiz.en: Even the president must obey the law.

quiz.q: {一円|いちえん}＿＿、{無駄|むだ}にしてはいけない。
quiz.en: Even a single yen should not be wasted.

quiz.q: {夏|なつ}＿＿、{山|やま}の{上|うえ}は{寒|さむ}い。
quiz.en: Even though it is summer, it is cold on the mountain.

structure: plain form + と{思|おも}いきや
explain: The speaker expected one thing, but the result was surprisingly different. It is a bit literary. It is similar to と{思|おも}ったら, but stresses the surprise more.

examples.jp: {晴|は}れると{思|おも}いきや、{急|きゅう}に{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ってきた。
examples.en: I thought it would be sunny, but suddenly it started raining.

examples.jp: {簡単|かんたん}な{試験|しけん}だと{思|おも}いきや、とても{難|むずか}しかった。
examples.en: I thought it was an easy test, but it was very hard.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{怒|おこ}ると{思|おも}いきや、{笑|わら}って{許|ゆる}してくれた。
examples.en: I thought he would be angry, but he laughed and forgave me.

quiz.q: もう{終|お}わった＿＿、まだ{半分|はんぶん}も{残|のこ}っていた。
quiz.en: I thought it was finished, but more than half was still left.

quiz.q: {高|たか}い＿＿、{意外|いがい}に{安|やす}かった。
quiz.en: I thought it would be expensive, but it was surprisingly cheap.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}が{優勝|ゆうしょう}する＿＿、{一回戦|いっかいせん}で{負|ま}けてしまった。
quiz.en: I thought he would win, but he lost in the first round.

structure: Noun / plain form + とはいえ
explain: Admits that A is true, but says B is different from what you would expect. It is like けれども but more formal. Compare といえども, which stresses "even this special case."

examples.jp: {春|はる}とはいえ、まだ{寒|さむ}い{日|ひ}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.en: Although it is spring, cold days continue.

examples.jp: {仕事|しごと}とはいえ、{毎日|まいにち}{残業|ざんぎょう}するのはつらい。
examples.en: It may be work, but working overtime every day is hard.

examples.jp: {慣|な}れたとはいえ、{敬語|けいご}はまだ{難|むずか}しい。
examples.en: Although I've gotten used to it, keigo is still hard.

quiz.q: {安|やす}かった＿＿、こんなにすぐ{壊|こわ}れるとは{思|おも}わなかった。
quiz.en: It was cheap, but I didn't think it would break so soon.

quiz.q: {日本|にほん}に{十年|じゅうねん}{住|す}んでいる＿＿、まだ{分|わ}からないことが{多|おお}い。
quiz.en: Although I have lived in Japan for ten years, there is still a lot I don't understand.

quiz.q: {自分|じぶん}で{決|き}めた＿＿、{会社|かいしゃ}を{辞|や}めるのは{寂|さび}しい。
quiz.en: Although I decided it myself, it's sad to leave the company.

structure: Verb (ます stem) / い-Adj / Noun + ながらも
explain: Means "although A, still B." It joins two things that seem to go against each other. It is a stronger, more written form of ながら meaning "although."

examples.jp: {狭|せま}いながらも{楽|たの}しい{我|わ}が{家|や}です。
examples.en: It's small, but it's our happy home.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{文句|もんく}を{言|い}いながらも、{手伝|てつだ}ってくれた。
examples.en: Although he complained, he helped me.

examples.jp: {子供|こども}ながらも、しっかりした{意見|いけん}を{持|も}っている。
examples.en: Although he's a child, he has firm opinions.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は{病気|びょうき}と{闘|たたか}い＿＿、{仕事|しごと}を{続|つづ}けた。
quiz.en: Although she was fighting an illness, she kept working.

quiz.q: {悪|わる}いと{知|し}り＿＿、{嘘|うそ}をついてしまった。
quiz.en: Although I knew it was wrong, I told a lie.

quiz.q: {小|ちい}さい＿＿、この{店|みせ}は{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
quiz.en: Although it's small, this shop is famous.

structure: Noun / Verb (ます stem) + ながらに（して）
explain: Means a state stays the same while something happens. It is used with fixed words like {涙|なみだ}ながらに, {生|う}まれながらに, いながらにして. Compare ながらも, which means "although."

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}は{涙|なみだ}ながらに{事故|じこ}のことを{語|かた}った。
examples.en: She talked about the accident in tears.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{生|う}まれながらに{音楽|おんがく}の{才能|さいのう}がある。
examples.en: He has had musical talent since birth.

examples.jp: インターネットで、{家|いえ}にいながらにして{買|か}い{物|もの}ができる。
examples.en: With the internet, you can shop without leaving home.

quiz.q: {母|はは}は{涙|なみだ}＿＿{私|わたし}を{見送|みおく}った。
quiz.en: My mother saw me off in tears.

quiz.q: {人|ひと}は{生|う}まれ＿＿{平等|びょうどう}だ。
quiz.en: People are born equal.

quiz.q: {昔|むかし}＿＿の{方法|ほうほう}で{酒|さけ}を{造|つく}っている。
quiz.en: They make sake using the same method as long ago.

structure: Noun + の / plain form + ところを
explain: Used in polite phrases to say "at a time when you are busy/tired, (thank you or sorry)." It also means "at the moment when someone was doing something."

examples.jp: お{忙|いそが}しいところを、ありがとうございます。
examples.en: Thank you for coming when you are so busy.

examples.jp: お{休|やす}みのところを{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありません。
examples.en: I'm sorry to bother you on your day off.

examples.jp: {泥棒|どろぼう}は{逃|に}げようとするところを{捕|つか}まった。
examples.en: The thief was caught just as he was trying to run away.

quiz.q: お{疲|つか}れの＿＿、{来|き}ていただいて{恐縮|きょうしゅく}です。
quiz.en: I'm very grateful you came when you're tired.

quiz.q: {寝|ね}ている＿＿{起|お}こしてしまって、ごめんなさい。
quiz.en: Sorry for waking you up while you were sleeping.

quiz.q: {本来|ほんらい}なら{伺|うかが}うべき＿＿、お{電話|でんわ}で{失礼|しつれい}します。
quiz.en: I should visit you in person, but please excuse me for calling instead.

structure: plain form + ものを
explain: Shows regret or complaint: "if you had done A, things would be fine, but you didn't." It is often used as ～ばいいものを or ～ば～ものを. Compare のに; ものを is more emotional and literary.

examples.jp: {早|はや}く{言|い}えば{手伝|てつだ}ったものを。
examples.en: If only you had told me sooner, I would have helped.

examples.jp: {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}めば{治|なお}るものを、{彼|かれ}は{飲|の}もうとしない。
examples.en: He'd get better if he took the medicine, but he won't.

examples.jp: {黙|だま}っていればいいものを、{余計|よけい}なことを{言|い}ってしまった。
examples.en: I should have kept quiet, but I said something unnecessary.

quiz.q: {一言|ひとこと}{謝|あやま}ればすむ＿＿、{彼|かれ}は{謝|あやま}らなかった。
quiz.en: A single apology would have settled it, but he didn't apologize.

quiz.q: もっと{早|はや}く{病院|びょういん}に{行|い}っていれば{助|たす}かった＿＿。
quiz.en: If only he had gone to the hospital earlier, he would have been saved.

quiz.q: {言|い}ってくれれば{車|くるま}で{迎|むか}えに{行|い}った＿＿。
quiz.en: If you had told me, I would have picked you up by car.

structure: Noun + とて
explain: Noun + とて means "even (this person/thing) is no exception." It is literary, like でも or だって. It is often used as {私|わたし}とて or {誰|だれ}とて.

examples.jp: {私|わたし}とて、{悲|かな}しくないわけではない。
examples.en: It's not that I'm not sad either.

examples.jp: {先生|せんせい}とて{人間|にんげん}だから、{間違|まちが}えることもある。
examples.en: Even teachers are human, so they make mistakes sometimes.

examples.jp: {誰|だれ}とて{死|し}ぬのは{怖|こわ}い。
examples.en: Anyone is afraid of dying.

quiz.q: {親|おや}＿＿、{子供|こども}の{気持|きも}ちが{全部|ぜんぶ}{分|わ}かるわけではない。
quiz.en: Even parents don't understand all of their child's feelings.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}＿＿、{最初|さいしょ}から{上手|じょうず}だったわけではない。
quiz.en: Even he wasn't good at it from the start.

quiz.q: {子供|こども}＿＿、{命|いのち}の{大切|たいせつ}さは{分|わ}かる。
quiz.en: Even a child understands how precious life is.

structure: Noun + であれ + Noun + であれ
explain: Means "whether A or B, it is the same." It is a formal way to say AでもBでも. A single であれ with a question word, like {何|なに}であれ, means "whatever it is."

examples.jp: {男|おとこ}であれ{女|おんな}であれ、{能力|のうりょく}があれば{採用|さいよう}する。
examples.en: Whether man or woman, we hire anyone with ability.

examples.jp: {晴|は}れであれ{雨|あめ}であれ、{試合|しあい}は{行|おこな}われる。
examples.en: Rain or shine, the match will be held.

examples.jp: {理由|りゆう}が{何|なん}であれ、{暴力|ぼうりょく}は{許|ゆる}されない。
examples.en: Whatever the reason, violence is not allowed.

quiz.q: {大人|おとな}＿＿{子供|こども}＿＿、ルールは{同|おな}じだ。
quiz.en: Whether adult or child, the rules are the same.

quiz.q: {誰|だれ}＿＿、{遅刻|ちこく}は{認|みと}めない。
quiz.en: No matter who it is, lateness is not accepted.

quiz.q: {仕事|しごと}＿＿{趣味|しゅみ}＿＿、{一生懸命|いっしょうけんめい}やるのが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
quiz.en: Whether work or a hobby, it's important to do your best.

structure: Noun + といい + Noun + といい
explain: Picks two examples to show that something is good or bad in every way. The speaker gives an evaluation at the end. Compare であれ～であれ, which means "whether A or B."

examples.jp: {色|いろ}といいデザインといい、この{服|ふく}は{完璧|かんぺき}だ。
examples.en: Both the color and the design make this outfit perfect.

examples.jp: {味|あじ}といい{値段|ねだん}といい、この{店|みせ}は{最高|さいこう}だ。
examples.en: In both taste and price, this restaurant is the best.

examples.jp: {兄|あに}といい{弟|おとうと}といい、あの{家|いえ}の{子|こ}はみんな{背|せ}が{高|たか}い。
examples.en: Both the older and younger brothers in that family are tall.

quiz.q: {景色|けしき}＿＿{料理|りょうり}＿＿、この{旅館|りょかん}は{素晴|すば}らしい。
options: といわず / といわず
quiz.en: Both the scenery and the food at this inn are wonderful.

quiz.q: {性格|せいかく}＿＿{顔|かお}＿＿、{彼|かれ}は{父親|ちちおや}にそっくりだ。
options: だろうが / だろうが
quiz.en: In both personality and looks, he is just like his father.

quiz.q: {態度|たいど}＿＿{言葉遣|ことばづか}い＿＿、あの{店員|てんいん}は{失礼|しつれい}だ。
quiz.en: Both his attitude and his way of speaking make that clerk rude.

meaning: all over ~ / not only A and B
structure: Noun + といわず + Noun + といわず
explain: Means "everywhere or all the time, not only A and B." It stresses that something happens in every part. Compare といい～といい, which gives an evaluation.

examples.jp: {手|て}といわず{顔|かお}といわず、{泥|どろ}だらけになった。
examples.en: My hands, my face, everything got covered in mud.

examples.jp: {昼|ひる}といわず{夜|よる}といわず、{工事|こうじ}の{音|おと}がうるさい。
examples.en: Day and night, the construction noise is loud.

examples.jp: {平日|へいじつ}といわず{週末|しゅうまつ}といわず、{彼|かれ}は{働|はたら}いている。
examples.en: He works on weekdays and weekends alike.

quiz.q: {壁|かべ}＿＿{床|ゆか}＿＿、{部屋中|へやじゅう}が{落書|らくが}きだらけだ。
options: といわず / といわず
quiz.en: Walls, floor, the whole room is covered in graffiti.

quiz.q: {朝|あさ}＿＿{晩|ばん}＿＿、{電話|でんわ}がかかってくる。
options: といわず / といわず
quiz.en: Morning and night, the phone keeps ringing.

quiz.q: {家|いえ}の{中|なか}＿＿{外|そと}＿＿、{猫|ねこ}の{毛|け}だらけだ。
options: といわず / といわず
quiz.en: Inside the house and out, it's covered in cat hair.

structure: Noun / Verb (dictionary) + なり + Noun / Verb + なり
explain: Gives two examples of possible choices and suggests picking one. It is often used to advise or request. Compare であれ～であれ, which means "whether A or B, it doesn't matter."

examples.jp: {分|わ}からなければ、{先生|せんせい}に{聞|き}くなり{辞書|じしょ}で{調|しら}べるなりしなさい。
examples.en: If you don't understand, ask the teacher or look it up in a dictionary.

examples.jp: {電話|でんわ}なりメールなりで{連絡|れんらく}してください。
examples.en: Please contact me by phone or email.

examples.jp: {疲|つか}れたら{休|やす}むなり{寝|ね}るなりしてください。
examples.en: If you're tired, take a break or go to sleep.

quiz.q: {困|こま}ったことがあれば、{親|おや}＿＿{友達|ともだち}＿＿に{相談|そうだん}しなさい。
options: といわず / といわず
quiz.en: If you have a problem, talk to your parents or a friend.

quiz.q: {暇|ひま}なら{本|ほん}を{読|よ}む＿＿{散歩|さんぽ}する＿＿したらどう？
quiz.en: If you're free, why not read a book or take a walk?

quiz.q: {意見|いけん}があれば、{会議|かいぎ}で{言|い}う＿＿{紙|かみ}に{書|か}く＿＿してください。
options: といわず / といわず
quiz.en: If you have an opinion, say it at the meeting or write it on paper.

structure: Verb A (ます stem) + つ + Verb B (ます stem) + つ
explain: Shows two opposite actions repeating, like going back and forth. It is used in fixed phrases such as {行|い}きつ{戻|もど}りつ, {持|も}ちつ{持|も}たれつ, and {抜|ぬ}きつ{抜|ぬ}かれつ.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{駅|えき}の{前|まえ}を{行|い}きつ{戻|もど}りつしていた。
examples.en: He was walking back and forth in front of the station.

examples.jp: {人|ひと}は{持|も}ちつ{持|も}たれつの{関係|かんけい}で{生|い}きている。
examples.en: People live by helping each other.

examples.jp: {二人|ふたり}は{抜|ぬ}きつ{抜|ぬ}かれつのレースをした。
examples.en: The two had a race where they kept overtaking each other.

quiz.q: {試合|しあい}は{追|お}い＿＿{追|お}われ＿＿の{展開|てんかい}となった。
quiz.en: The match became a back-and-forth chase.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は{渡|わた}そうか{迷|まよ}って、{部屋|へや}の{中|なか}を{行|い}き＿＿{戻|もど}り＿＿していた。
quiz.en: Unsure whether to give it, she paced back and forth in the room.

quiz.q: {近所|きんじょ}の{人|ひと}とは{持|も}ち＿＿{持|も}たれ＿＿で{助|たす}け{合|あ}っている。
quiz.en: We help our neighbors and they help us in return.

structure: Verb (volitional) + が / と; い-Adj かろう + が
explain: Means "no matter what happens, the result doesn't change." It is often used with question words like {何|なに}を, どこで, or {誰|だれ}が. It is stronger than ても.

examples.jp: {何|なに}を{言|い}われようが、{私|わたし}の{気持|きも}ちは{変|か}わらない。
examples.en: No matter what anyone says, my feelings won't change.

examples.jp: どんなに{寒|さむ}かろうと、{彼|かれ}は{毎朝|まいあさ}{走|はし}る。
examples.en: No matter how cold it is, he runs every morning.

examples.jp: {誰|だれ}が{来|こ}ようと、ドアを{開|あ}けてはいけない。
examples.en: No matter who comes, don't open the door.

quiz.q: {周|まわ}りに{反対|はんたい}され＿＿、{私|わたし}はこの{道|みち}を{進|すす}む。
quiz.en: Even if people around me oppose me, I'll follow this path.

quiz.q: どこに＿＿、{君|きみ}の{自由|じゆう}だ。
quiz.en: Wherever you live, it's up to you.

quiz.q: どんなに＿＿、{必要|ひつよう}なものは{買|か}う。
quiz.en: However expensive it is, I'll buy what I need.

structure: Verb (volitional) + が + Verb (dictionary) + まいが
explain: Means "whether you do it or not, the result is the same." The same verb is used twice. ようと～まいと is the same meaning.

examples.jp: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ろうが{降|ふ}るまいが、{試合|しあい}は{行|おこな}われる。
examples.en: Whether it rains or not, the match will be held.

examples.jp: {君|きみ}が{行|い}こうが{行|い}くまいが、{私|わたし}は{行|い}く。
examples.en: Whether you go or not, I'm going.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}が{来|こ}ようと{来|く}るまいと、{会議|かいぎ}は{始|はじ}める。
examples.en: Whether he comes or not, we'll start the meeting.

quiz.q: {信|しん}じよう＿＿{信|しん}じ＿＿、これは{本当|ほんとう}の{話|はなし}だ。
quiz.en: Whether you believe it or not, this is a true story.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}が{賛成|さんせい}しよう＿＿、{計画|けいかく}は{進|すす}める。
quiz.en: Whether he agrees or not, we'll go ahead with the plan.

quiz.q: {試験|しけん}に{受|う}かろう＿＿、{最後|さいご}まで{頑張|がんば}ろう。
quiz.en: Whether we pass the exam or not, let's do our best to the end.

meaning: so as not to ~ / trying not to ~
structure: Verb (dictionary) + まいと（して）
explain: Shows a strong effort to avoid something. It is a written way to say ないように. Compare まい alone, which means "will not" or "probably not."

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{泣|な}くまいと{歯|は}を{食|く}いしばった。
examples.en: He clenched his teeth, trying not to cry.

examples.jp: {遅刻|ちこく}するまいと、{朝早|あさはや}く{家|いえ}を{出|で}た。
examples.en: I left home early so as not to be late.

examples.jp: {同|おな}じ{失敗|しっぱい}を{繰|く}り{返|かえ}すまいと{心|こころ}に{決|き}めた。
examples.en: I made up my mind never to repeat the same mistake.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は{笑|わら}う＿＿、{必死|ひっし}にこらえた。
quiz.en: She tried hard not to laugh.

quiz.q: {負|ま}ける＿＿、{毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}した。
quiz.en: I practiced every day so as not to lose.

quiz.q: {秘密|ひみつ}を{知|し}られ＿＿、{彼|かれ}は{何|なに}も{話|はな}さなかった。
quiz.en: So as not to let the secret out, he said nothing.

structure: Verb (ない form minus ない) + んがため（に）  (する → せんがため)
explain: Shows a strong purpose, often with great effort. It is very formal. It is stronger than ために and is not used for small, everyday goals.

examples.jp: {夢|ゆめ}を{実現|じつげん}せんがため、{彼|かれ}は{海外|かいがい}に{渡|わた}った。
examples.en: To make his dream come true, he went overseas.

examples.jp: {勝|か}たんがために、{選手|せんしゅ}たちは{厳|きび}しい{練習|れんしゅう}に{耐|た}えた。
examples.en: In order to win, the players endured hard training.

examples.jp: {生|い}きんがために{働|はたら}く。
examples.en: I work in order to live.

quiz.q: {真実|しんじつ}を{明|あき}らかにせ＿＿、{記者|きしゃ}は{調査|ちょうさ}を{続|つづ}けた。
quiz.en: In order to reveal the truth, the reporter kept investigating.

quiz.q: {合格|ごうかく}せ＿＿、{寝|ね}る{間|ま}も{惜|お}しんで{勉強|べんきょう}した。
quiz.en: In order to pass, I studied even giving up sleep.

quiz.q: {子供|こども}を{守|まも}ら＿＿、{母親|ははおや}は{火|ひ}の{中|なか}に{飛|と}び{込|こ}んだ。
quiz.en: In order to protect her child, the mother jumped into the fire.

structure: Verb (dictionary) + べく  (する → するべく / すべく)
explain: A formal way to say "in order to." It is used in writing and news. It is not used with requests or commands. Compare んがため, which is even stronger.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{医者|いしゃ}になるべく、{毎日|まいにち}{勉強|べんきょう}している。
examples.en: He studies every day in order to become a doctor.

examples.jp: {問題|もんだい}を{解決|かいけつ}すべく、{会議|かいぎ}が{開|ひら}かれた。
examples.en: A meeting was held to solve the problem.

examples.jp: {家族|かぞく}を{支|ささ}えるべく、{彼女|かのじょ}は{働|はたら}き{始|はじ}めた。
examples.en: She started working to support her family.

quiz.q: {新|あたら}しい{市場|しじょう}を{開拓|かいたく}す＿＿、{社員|しゃいん}を{海外|かいがい}に{送|おく}った。
quiz.en: In order to open up new markets, the company sent employees overseas.

quiz.q: {記録|きろく}を{更新|こうしん}する＿＿、{彼|かれ}は{練習|れんしゅう}を{重|かさ}ねた。
quiz.en: He practiced hard in order to break the record.

quiz.q: {被災地|ひさいち}を{支援|しえん}す＿＿、{募金|ぼきん}{活動|かつどう}が{始|はじ}まった。
quiz.en: A fundraising campaign began to support the disaster area.

structure: Verb (dictionary) + べからず / べからざる + Noun
explain: A very strong "must not," mostly on signs and in rules. べからざる is used before a noun, meaning "should not / cannot." する becomes すべからず.

examples.jp: ここにごみを{捨|す}てるべからず。
examples.en: Do not throw garbage here.

examples.jp: {芝生|しばふ}に{入|はい}るべからず。
examples.en: Keep off the grass.

examples.jp: それは{許|ゆる}すべからざる{行為|こうい}だ。
examples.en: That is an unforgivable act.

quiz.q: {関係者|かんけいしゃ}{以外|いがい}、{立|た}ち{入|い}る＿＿。
quiz.en: Authorized personnel only. Do not enter.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}はこのチームに{欠|か}く＿＿{人物|じんぶつ}だ。
quiz.en: He is an indispensable member of this team.

quiz.q: {働|はたら}かざる{者|もの}、{食|く}う＿＿。
quiz.en: He who does not work shall not eat.

structure: Noun + にあるまじき / として + あるまじき + Noun
explain: Means behavior that is unacceptable for someone in a certain role. It is usually used as ～にあるまじき{行為|こうい}. It is a strong criticism.

examples.jp: それは{教師|きょうし}にあるまじき{行為|こうい}だ。
examples.en: That is unacceptable behavior for a teacher.

examples.jp: {政治家|せいじか}としてあるまじき{発言|はつげん}だ。
examples.en: That is a remark a politician should never make.

examples.jp: {人|ひと}として{許|ゆる}すまじき{犯罪|はんざい}だ。
examples.en: It is a crime that should never be forgiven.

quiz.q: {患者|かんじゃ}の{情報|じょうほう}を{漏|も}らすなど、{医者|いしゃ}にある＿＿ことだ。
quiz.en: Leaking patient information is unacceptable for a doctor.

quiz.q: {警察官|けいさつかん}にある＿＿{不正|ふせい}が{発覚|はっかく}した。
quiz.en: Misconduct unacceptable for a police officer came to light.

quiz.q: {子供|こども}を{見捨|みす}てるなど、{親|おや}としてある＿＿ことだ。
quiz.en: Abandoning a child is unthinkable for a parent.

meaning: will surely ~ / cannot help but cause ~
structure: Verb (ない form minus ない) + ずにはおかない  (する → せずにはおかない)
explain: Something naturally causes a feeling or reaction, or someone is determined to do something. It is often used with feelings like {感動|かんどう}させる. Compare ずにはすまない, which means "must do it because of duty."

examples.jp: この{映画|えいが}は{見|み}る{人|ひと}を{感動|かんどう}させずにはおかない。
examples.en: This movie is sure to move everyone who sees it.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}の{発言|はつげん}は{議論|ぎろん}を{呼|よ}ばずにはおかないだろう。
examples.en: His remark is sure to cause debate.

examples.jp: {今度|こんど}こそ{真実|しんじつ}を{話|はな}させずにはおかない。
examples.en: This time I will make him tell the truth, no matter what.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}の{歌声|うたごえ}は{聞|き}く{人|ひと}を{魅了|みりょう}せ＿＿。
quiz.en: Her singing voice is sure to charm everyone who hears it.

quiz.q: その{事件|じけん}は{社会|しゃかい}に{大|おお}きな{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}え＿＿だろう。
quiz.en: That incident will surely have a big impact on society.

quiz.q: {必|かなら}ず{犯人|はんにん}を{見|み}つけ{出|だ}さ＿＿。
quiz.en: I'll find the criminal, no matter what.

structure: Verb (ない form minus ない) + ずにはすまない / ないではすまない
explain: Because of the situation, rules, or duty, you cannot avoid doing something. Often used with {謝|あやま}る or {払|はら}う. Compare ずにはおかない, which is about strong will or a natural effect.

examples.jp: {人|ひと}のものを{壊|こわ}したのだから、{弁償|べんしょう}せずにはすまない。
examples.en: I broke someone's thing, so I have to pay for it.

examples.jp: こんなミスをしたら、{上司|じょうし}に{報告|ほうこく}しないではすまない。
examples.en: After such a mistake, I can't avoid reporting it to my boss.

examples.jp: {約束|やくそく}を{破|やぶ}ったのだから、{謝|あやま}らずにはすまないだろう。
examples.en: You broke your promise, so you will have to apologize.

quiz.q: {会社|かいしゃ}に{損害|そんがい}を{与|あた}えたのだから、{責任|せきにん}を{取|と}ら＿＿。
quiz.en: Since you caused damage to the company, you must take responsibility.

quiz.q: {部長|ぶちょう}の{車|くるま}にぶつけたのだから、{謝|あやま}ら＿＿だろう。
quiz.en: You hit the manager's car, so you'll have to apologize.

quiz.q: {法律|ほうりつ}が{変|か}わった{以上|いじょう}、{制度|せいど}を{見直|みなお}さ＿＿。
quiz.en: Now that the law has changed, the system has to be reviewed.

structure: Noun (feeling) + を{禁|きん}じ{得|え}ない
explain: A formal way to say you cannot hold back a feeling, like anger, tears, or surprise. It is used with feeling nouns such as {怒|いか}り, {涙|なみだ}, {同情|どうじょう}. It is not used for actions.

examples.jp: その{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いて、{涙|なみだ}を{禁|きん}じ{得|え}なかった。
examples.en: I could not hold back my tears when I heard that story.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}の{無責任|むせきにん}な{態度|たいど}に{怒|いか}りを{禁|きん}じ{得|え}ない。
examples.en: I can't help feeling angry at his irresponsible attitude.

examples.jp: {被害者|ひがいしゃ}の{家族|かぞく}には{同情|どうじょう}を{禁|きん}じ{得|え}ない。
examples.en: I can't help feeling sympathy for the victims' families.

quiz.q: {突然|とつぜん}の{知|し}らせに{驚|おどろ}き＿＿。
options: を{余儀|よぎ}なくされる
quiz.en: I can't help being surprised by the sudden news.

quiz.q: {政府|せいふ}の{対応|たいおう}には{疑問|ぎもん}＿＿。
quiz.en: I can't help having doubts about the government's response.

quiz.q: {子供|こども}たちの{笑顔|えがお}を{見|み}て、{喜|よろこ}び＿＿。
options: を{余儀|よぎ}なくさせた
を{皮切|かわき}りにした
を{禁|きん}じ{得|え}なかった
quiz.en: Seeing the children's smiles, I couldn't hold back my joy.

structure: Noun + を{余儀|よぎ}なくされる / を{余儀|よぎ}なくさせる
explain: Someone is forced to do something they did not want because of circumstances. される is the passive (be forced); させる means something forces it. Often used with nouns like {中止|ちゅうし} or {変更|へんこう}.

examples.jp: {大雨|おおあめ}で、{試合|しあい}は{中止|ちゅうし}を{余儀|よぎ}なくされた。
examples.en: Because of heavy rain, the match was forced to be canceled.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}はけがで{引退|いんたい}を{余儀|よぎ}なくされた。
examples.en: He was forced to retire due to an injury.

examples.jp: {不況|ふきょう}が{会社|かいしゃ}に{人員|じんいん}{削減|さくげん}を{余儀|よぎ}なくさせた。
examples.en: The recession forced the company to cut staff.

quiz.q: {台風|たいふう}のため、{飛行機|ひこうき}は{着陸|ちゃくりく}{地|ち}の{変更|へんこう}＿＿。
options: を{余儀|よぎ}なくされた
を{禁|きん}じ{得|え}なかった
をものともしなかった
quiz.en: Because of the typhoon, the plane was forced to change its landing site.

quiz.q: {資金|しきん}{不足|ぶそく}で、{計画|けいかく}は{延期|えんき}＿＿。
options: を{余儀|よぎ}なくされた
を{皮切|かわき}りにした
quiz.en: Due to a lack of funds, the plan was forced to be postponed.

quiz.q: {病気|びょうき}が{彼|かれ}に{長期|ちょうき}{入院|にゅういん}＿＿。
options: を{余儀|よぎ}なくさせた
を{余儀|よぎ}なくされた
quiz.en: His illness forced him into a long hospital stay.

structure: Verb (て form) + やまない
explain: Shows a strong feeling that continues, like hoping or loving. It is used with verbs such as {願|ねが}う, {祈|いの}る, {愛|あい}する. It is formal and often used in speeches.

examples.jp: {皆様|みなさま}のご{健康|けんこう}を{願|ねが}ってやみません。
examples.en: I sincerely wish you all good health.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{生涯|しょうがい}、{故郷|こきょう}を{愛|あい}してやまなかった。
examples.en: He loved his hometown all his life.

examples.jp: {平和|へいわ}な{世界|せかい}を{望|のぞ}んでやまない。
examples.en: I truly hope for a peaceful world.

quiz.q: お{二人|ふたり}の{幸|しあわ}せを{祈|いの}って＿＿。
quiz.en: I sincerely pray for your happiness.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は{子供|こども}たちに{愛|あい}されて＿＿{先生|せんせい}だった。
quiz.en: She was a teacher whom the children loved deeply.

quiz.q: {皆|みな}さんのご{活躍|かつやく}を{期待|きたい}して＿＿。
quiz.en: I truly look forward to your success.

structure: Verb (dictionary) + までもない / までもなく
explain: Something is so obvious or simple that you don't need to do it. Often used with {言|い}う, {説明|せつめい}する. {言|い}うまでもなく means "needless to say."

examples.jp: そんな{簡単|かんたん}なことは、{説明|せつめい}するまでもない。
examples.en: Such a simple thing doesn't need explaining.

examples.jp: {言|い}うまでもなく、{健康|けんこう}は{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.en: Needless to say, health is important.

examples.jp: {近|ちか}いから、{車|くるま}で{行|い}くまでもない。
examples.en: It's close, so there's no need to go by car.

quiz.q: この{程度|ていど}のかすり{傷|きず}なら、{病院|びょういん}に{行|い}く＿＿。
quiz.en: With an injury this small, there's no need to go to the hospital.

quiz.q: {言|い}う＿＿、{試験|しけん}{中|ちゅう}の{携帯|けいたい}{使用|しよう}は{禁止|きんし}です。
quiz.en: Needless to say, phone use during the exam is prohibited.

quiz.q: {電話|でんわ}ですむことなので、わざわざ{会|あ}いに{行|い}く＿＿。
quiz.en: It can be handled by phone, so there's no need to go and meet in person.

structure: Verb (dictionary) + までだ / Verb (た form) + までのことだ
explain: With dictionary form, it means "if that fails, I'll simply do this other thing." With た form, it means "I only did this, nothing more." It shows a calm, decided feeling.

examples.jp: バスがないなら、{歩|ある}いて{帰|かえ}るまでだ。
examples.en: If there's no bus, I'll just walk home.

examples.jp: {反対|はんたい}されても、{一人|ひとり}でやるまでだ。
examples.en: Even if they oppose me, I'll just do it alone.

examples.jp: {当然|とうぜん}のことをしたまでです。
examples.en: I only did what was natural.

quiz.q: {今年|ことし}だめなら、{来年|らいねん}また{受験|じゅけん}する＿＿。
quiz.en: If I fail this year, I'll just take the exam again next year.

quiz.q: お{礼|れい}なんていりません。{仕事|しごと}をした＿＿ですから。
quiz.en: No need to thank me. I was only doing my job.

quiz.q: {誰|だれ}も{手伝|てつだ}ってくれないなら、{自分|じぶん}でやる＿＿。
quiz.en: If nobody will help me, I'll just do it myself.

structure: Verb (dictionary) / Noun / Adj + に{越|こ}したことはない
explain: Means "it's better if it is so," often used for common sense advice. It is softer than べきだ. It is often used with ほうがいい ideas like {安|やす}い, {早|はや}い, {注意|ちゅうい}する.

examples.jp: {値段|ねだん}は{安|やす}いに{越|こ}したことはない。
examples.en: Cheaper is always better.

examples.jp: {念|ねん}のため、{確認|かくにん}するに{越|こ}したことはない。
examples.en: Just in case, it's best to check.

examples.jp: {健康|けんこう}に{越|こ}したことはない。
examples.en: Nothing is better than good health.

quiz.q: {念|ねん}のため、{用心|ようじん}する＿＿。
options: に{越|こ}したことはない
quiz.en: Just to be safe, it's best to be careful.

quiz.q: {早|はや}めに{準備|じゅんび}する＿＿。
options: に{越|こ}したことはない
quiz.en: It's best to prepare early.

quiz.q: {貯金|ちょきん}は{多|おお}い＿＿が、{使|つか}うことも{大切|たいせつ}だ。
options: に{越|こ}したことはない
quiz.en: Having more savings is better, but spending is also important.

structure: Verb (dictionary) + にたえない / にたえる; Noun (feeling) + にたえない
explain: {見|み}る/{聞|き}くにたえない means "too bad to watch or listen to." Noun + にたえない (like {感謝|かんしゃ}にたえない) means "I feel deeply." にたえる means "worth (watching/reading)."

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}の{悪口|わるぐち}は{聞|き}くにたえない。
examples.en: His insults are unbearable to listen to.

examples.jp: {皆様|みなさま}のご{支援|しえん}に{感謝|かんしゃ}にたえません。
examples.en: I am deeply grateful for your support.

examples.jp: これは{大人|おとな}の{鑑賞|かんしょう}にたえる{作品|さくひん}だ。
examples.en: This work is worth appreciating even for adults.

quiz.q: {事故|じこ}{現場|げんば}は{見|み}る＿＿{状態|じょうたい}だった。
quiz.en: The accident scene was too terrible to look at.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}の{歌|うた}は{下手|へた}すぎて、{聞|き}く＿＿。
options: に{越|こ}したことはない
quiz.en: His singing is so bad it's unbearable to listen to.

quiz.q: {多|おお}くの{方|かた}のご{協力|きょうりょく}をいただき、{感謝|かんしゃ}＿＿。
quiz.en: I am deeply grateful for so many people's cooperation.

structure: Verb (dictionary) / Noun + に{足|た}る + Noun
explain: Means something is worth or good enough for an action, like trust or respect. に{足|た}らない means "not worth it." Compare にたえる, which is mostly about watching or reading.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{信頼|しんらい}するに{足|た}る{人物|じんぶつ}だ。
examples.en: He is a person worthy of trust.

examples.jp: それは{取|と}るに{足|た}らない{問題|もんだい}だ。
examples.en: That is a trivial problem.

examples.jp: {満足|まんぞく}に{足|た}る{結果|けっか}が{出|で}た。
examples.en: We got a satisfying result.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は{尊敬|そんけい}する＿＿{先輩|せんぱい}だ。
quiz.en: She is a senior worthy of respect.

quiz.q: そんな{取|と}る＿＿ことで{悩|なや}む{必要|ひつよう}はない。
quiz.en: You don't need to worry about such a trivial thing.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}の{話|はなし}には{信用|しんよう}する＿＿{証拠|しょうこ}がない。
quiz.en: There is no evidence that makes his story worth believing.

structure: Noun / Verb (dictionary) + にかたくない
explain: Means "it is not hard to imagine or understand." It is used with {想像|そうぞう}, {理解|りかい}, {察|さっ}する. It is formal and used in writing.

examples.jp: {家族|かぞく}を{失|うしな}った{彼|かれ}の{悲|かな}しみは、{想像|そうぞう}にかたくない。
examples.en: It is easy to imagine his sadness at losing his family.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}が{怒|おこ}った{理由|りゆう}は{理解|りかい}にかたくない。
examples.en: It is easy to understand why she got angry.

examples.jp: {親|おや}の{心配|しんぱい}は{察|さっ}するにかたくない。
examples.en: It is easy to guess how worried the parents are.

quiz.q: {一人|ひとり}で{子供|こども}を{育|そだ}てる{苦労|くろう}は、{想像|そうぞう}＿＿。
quiz.en: The hardship of raising a child alone is easy to imagine.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}がどれほど{努力|どりょく}したかは、{察|さっ}する＿＿。
options: に{越|こ}したことはない
quiz.en: It is easy to guess how hard he worked.

quiz.q: {優勝|ゆうしょう}した{時|とき}の{喜|よろこ}びは{想像|そうぞう}＿＿。
options: を{余儀|よぎ}なくされる
quiz.en: It is easy to imagine the joy of winning.

structure: Noun + の / Verb (dictionary) + かたわら
explain: Someone does a second activity besides their main job over a long time. Compare ながら, which is two actions at the same moment, and がてら, which is one trip with two purposes.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{会社|かいしゃ}で{働|はたら}くかたわら、{小説|しょうせつ}を{書|か}いている。
examples.en: While working at a company, he also writes novels.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}は{子育|こそだ}てのかたわら、{大学|だいがく}で{勉強|べんきょう}している。
examples.en: While raising children, she also studies at university.

examples.jp: {父|ちち}は{教師|きょうし}をするかたわら、{畑|はたけ}で{野菜|やさい}を{作|つく}っている。
examples.en: While working as a teacher, my father also grows vegetables.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{医者|いしゃ}の{仕事|しごと}の＿＿、ボランティア{活動|かつどう}もしている。
quiz.en: Besides his work as a doctor, he also does volunteer work.

quiz.q: {母|はは}は{家事|かじ}の＿＿、{翻訳|ほんやく}の{仕事|しごと}をしている。
quiz.en: Alongside the housework, my mother also does translation work.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は{大学|だいがく}に{通|かよ}う＿＿、モデルとして{活躍|かつやく}している。
quiz.en: While attending university, she also works as a model.

meaning: while ~ (doing two things on one trip)
structure: Noun / Verb (ます stem) + がてら
explain: While doing A, you also do B, usually on the same trip. A is often a walk or outing, like {散歩|さんぽ}がてら. It is casual. Compare かたがた, which is formal.

examples.jp: {散歩|さんぽ}がてら、パンを{買|か}いに{行|い}った。
examples.en: I went to buy bread while taking a walk.

examples.jp: {駅|えき}まで{送|おく}りがてら、{本屋|ほんや}に{寄|よ}った。
examples.en: While seeing her off to the station, I stopped by a bookstore.

examples.jp: {買|か}い{物|もの}がてら、{友達|ともだち}の{家|いえ}に{寄|よ}った。
examples.en: I dropped by a friend's house while out shopping.

quiz.q: {天気|てんき}がいいので、{散歩|さんぽ}＿＿{郵便局|ゆうびんきょく}に{行|い}ってきます。
quiz.en: The weather's nice, so I'll go to the post office while taking a walk.

quiz.q: {花見|はなみ}＿＿、{公園|こうえん}でお{弁当|べんとう}を{食|た}べた。
quiz.en: While enjoying the cherry blossoms, we ate lunch in the park.

quiz.q: {運動|うんどう}＿＿、{歩|ある}いて{会社|かいしゃ}に{通|かよ}っている。
quiz.en: I walk to work, which also gives me exercise.

structure: Noun + かたがた
explain: A formal way to say you do one action with two purposes, like visiting to greet and also to thank. Used with nouns like お{礼|れい}, ご{挨拶|あいさつ}, お{見舞|みま}い. Often in letters and business.

examples.jp: お{礼|れい}かたがた、ご{挨拶|あいさつ}に{伺|うかが}いました。
examples.en: I came to greet you and also to thank you.

examples.jp: ご{報告|ほうこく}かたがた、お{礼|れい}を{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
examples.en: I'd like to report to you and also thank you.

examples.jp: お{見舞|みま}いかたがた、{先生|せんせい}のお{宅|たく}を{訪|たず}ねた。
examples.en: I visited my teacher's home to see how he was and also to say hello.

quiz.q: {近況|きんきょう}{報告|ほうこく}＿＿、お{手紙|てがみ}を{差|さ}し{上|あ}げます。
quiz.en: I'm writing to you to let you know how I'm doing as well.

quiz.q: {就職|しゅうしょく}のご{報告|ほうこく}＿＿、{恩師|おんし}を{訪|たず}ねた。
quiz.en: I visited my former teacher to report my new job and to say hello.

quiz.q: お{詫|わ}び＿＿、ご{説明|せつめい}に{参|まい}りました。
quiz.en: I have come to apologize and also to explain.

structure: Verb (dictionary) / この / あの + {始末|しまつ}だ
explain: After a series of bad things, it finally ended in an even worse result. It shows the speaker's criticism or disappointment. Compare あげく, which is similar but less emotional.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{遅刻|ちこく}ばかりして、ついには{無断|むだん}で{休|やす}む{始末|しまつ}だ。
examples.en: He was always late, and in the end he even skipped work without telling anyone.

examples.jp: {弟|おとうと}はお{金|かね}を{使|つか}い{果|は}たし、{私|わたし}に{借|か}りに{来|く}る{始末|しまつ}だ。
examples.en: My brother spent all his money and even came to borrow from me.

examples.jp: {何度|なんど}{注意|ちゅうい}しても{直|なお}らず、この{始末|しまつ}だ。
examples.en: I warned him many times, but nothing changed, and now look at this.

quiz.q: {息子|むすこ}は{勉強|べんきょう}しないで、{最後|さいご}には{学校|がっこう}を{辞|や}める＿＿。
quiz.en: My son didn't study, and in the end he even quit school.

quiz.q: {飲|の}みすぎて、{駅|えき}で{寝|ね}てしまう＿＿だった。
quiz.en: I drank too much and ended up falling asleep at the station.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}はうそを{重|かさ}ね、とうとう{友達|ともだち}を{全員|ぜんいん}{失|うしな}う＿＿。
quiz.en: He kept lying and finally lost all his friends.

structure: Noun + ずくめ
explain: Means something is filled with only one kind of thing. It is often used with good things like いいこと or ごちそう, and with {黒|くろ} for color. Compare まみれ, which is for dirty things on a surface.

examples.jp: {今年|ことし}はいいことずくめの{一年|いちねん}だった。
examples.en: This year was full of good things.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}はいつも{黒|くろ}ずくめの{服|ふく}を{着|き}ている。
examples.en: He always wears all black.

examples.jp: {結婚式|けっこんしき}はごちそうずくめだった。
examples.en: The wedding was full of great food.

quiz.q: {昇進|しょうしん}に{結婚|けっこん}と、{最近|さいきん}はいいこと＿＿だ。
quiz.en: With a promotion and a wedding, lately everything has been good.

quiz.q: {黒|くろ}＿＿の{男|おとこ}が{立|た}っていた。
quiz.en: A man dressed all in black was standing there.

quiz.q: この{会社|かいしゃ}は{規則|きそく}＿＿で{窮屈|きゅうくつ}だ。
quiz.en: This company is full of rules and feels stifling.

structure: Noun + まみれ
explain: Means something is covered all over with a dirty or unpleasant thing, like mud, sweat, or blood. Compare だらけ, which can also mean "full of" mistakes or problems.

examples.jp: {子供|こども}たちは{泥|どろ}まみれになって{遊|あそ}んだ。
examples.en: The kids played and got covered in mud.

examples.jp: {夏|なつ}の{工事|こうじ}{現場|げんば}で、{汗|あせ}まみれになって{働|はたら}いた。
examples.en: I worked at the construction site in summer, drenched in sweat.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{血|ち}まみれで{倒|たお}れていた。
examples.en: He was lying there covered in blood.

quiz.q: {大掃除|おおそうじ}をしたら、{手|て}がほこり＿＿になった。
quiz.en: After the big cleaning, my hands were covered in dust.

quiz.q: {雨|あめ}の{中|なか}で{試合|しあい}をして、{選手|せんしゅ}たちは{泥|どろ}＿＿だった。
quiz.en: After playing in the rain, the players were covered in mud.

quiz.q: {借金|しゃっきん}＿＿の{生活|せいかつ}から{抜|ぬ}け{出|だ}したい。
quiz.en: I want to escape a life buried in debt.

structure: Noun + めく / めいた + Noun
explain: Means something starts to have the feeling of a noun, like {春|はる}めく (feel like spring). めいた + noun means "sounding like," as in {皮肉|ひにく}めいた{言葉|ことば}.

examples.jp: {日差|ひざ}しが{暖|あたた}かくなって、{春|はる}めいてきた。
examples.en: The sunshine has gotten warm, and it's starting to feel like spring.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{冗談|じょうだん}めいた{口調|くちょう}で{話|はな}した。
examples.en: He spoke in a joking tone.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}の{言葉|ことば}には{皮肉|ひにく}めいたところがある。
examples.en: There is something sarcastic about her words.

quiz.q: {木々|きぎ}の{葉|は}が{色|いろ}づき、すっかり{秋|あき}＿＿きた。
quiz.en: The leaves have changed color, and it really feels like autumn now.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{言|い}い{訳|わけ}＿＿ことは{一言|ひとこと}も{言|い}わなかった。
quiz.en: He didn't say a single word that sounded like an excuse.

quiz.q: {謎|なぞ}＿＿{手紙|てがみ}が{届|とど}いた。
quiz.en: A mysterious-sounding letter arrived.

structure: Noun / な-Adj stem / い-Adj stem + ぶる
explain: Someone acts as if they are something they are not, usually in an annoying way. Common words are {偉|えら}ぶる, {上品|じょうひん}ぶる, いい{子|こ}ぶる. It has a negative feeling. Compare めく, which is about natural signs.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{新人|しんじん}なのに{先輩|せんぱい}ぶっている。
examples.en: He's a newcomer but acts like a senior.

examples.jp: {先生|せんせい}の{前|まえ}だけいい{子|こ}ぶるのはやめなさい。
examples.en: Stop acting like a good kid only in front of the teacher.

examples.jp: {偉|えら}ぶった{態度|たいど}は{嫌|きら}われる。
examples.en: People dislike a self-important attitude.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は{何|なん}でも{知|し}っているかのように{学者|がくしゃ}＿＿いる。
quiz.en: She acts like a scholar, as if she knows everything.

quiz.q: {上品|じょうひん}＿＿{話|はな}し{方|かた}が{鼻|はな}につく。
quiz.en: Her affected, upper-class way of speaking is irritating.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{部長|ぶちょう}になってから{偉|えら}＿＿ようになった。
quiz.en: He started acting important after becoming manager.

structure: Verb (dictionary) / Noun + の + きらいがある
explain: Someone has a tendency to do something bad or undesirable. It is used for criticism. Compare がちだ, which is softer and more common in daily speech.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{物事|ものごと}を{大|おお}げさに{言|い}うきらいがある。
examples.en: He tends to exaggerate things.

examples.jp: {最近|さいきん}の{若者|わかもの}は{失敗|しっぱい}を{恐|おそ}れるきらいがある。
examples.en: Young people today tend to be afraid of failure.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}は{何|なん}でも{一人|ひとり}で{決|き}めてしまうきらいがある。
examples.en: She tends to decide everything on her own.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{人|ひと}の{意見|いけん}を{聞|き}かない＿＿。
quiz.en: He tends not to listen to others' opinions.

quiz.q: {政府|せいふ}は{問題|もんだい}を{先送|さきおく}りにする＿＿。
quiz.en: The government tends to postpone problems.

quiz.q: {父|ちち}は{少|すこ}し{頑固|がんこ}な＿＿。
quiz.en: My father tends to be a bit stubborn.

structure: Noun + の + ごとき + Noun / ごとく + Verb; Noun + ごとき (humble or scornful)
explain: A formal way to say ような or ように. ごとく is used before a verb and ごとき before a noun. Noun + ごとき (without の) can also look down on someone, like {私|わたし}ごとき "someone like me."

examples.jp: {時間|じかん}は{矢|や}のごとく{過|す}ぎていく。
examples.en: Time flies like an arrow.

examples.jp: {前述|ぜんじゅつ}のごとく、{計画|けいかく}は{変更|へんこう}された。
examples.en: As stated above, the plan was changed.

examples.jp: {私|わたし}ごときに、そんな{大役|たいやく}は{務|つと}まりません。
examples.en: Someone like me can't handle such an important role.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{何事|なにごと}もなかったかの＿＿{笑|わら}っていた。
quiz.en: He was smiling as if nothing had happened.

quiz.q: {夢|ゆめ}の＿＿{日々|ひび}が{終|お}わった。
quiz.en: The dreamlike days came to an end.

quiz.q: お{前|まえ}＿＿に{負|ま}けるわけがない。
quiz.en: There's no way I'd lose to the likes of you.

structure: Verb (ない form) + までも
explain: Means "even if you can't do the full thing, at least do a smaller thing." The second part is often a lower goal with べきだ or ほしい. Compare までもない, which means "no need to."

examples.jp: {毎日|まいにち}とは{言|い}わないまでも、{週|しゅう}に{一度|いちど}は{電話|でんわ}してほしい。
examples.en: Not every day, but I want you to call at least once a week.

examples.jp: {優勝|ゆうしょう}できないまでも、{決勝|けっしょう}には{進|すす}みたい。
examples.en: Even if we can't win, I want to reach the final.

examples.jp: {謝|あやま}らないまでも、{説明|せつめい}ぐらいはするべきだ。
examples.en: Even if you don't apologize, you should at least explain.

quiz.q: {完璧|かんぺき}とは{言|い}わ＿＿、もう{少|すこ}し{丁寧|ていねい}に{書|か}いてほしい。
quiz.en: I don't ask for perfect, but I want you to write a bit more carefully.

quiz.q: {手伝|てつだ}わ＿＿、{邪魔|じゃま}はしないでほしい。
quiz.en: Even if you don't help, at least don't get in the way.

quiz.q: {満点|まんてん}は{取|と}れ＿＿、{合格|ごうかく}{点|てん}は{取|と}りたい。
quiz.en: Even if I can't get full marks, I want a passing score.

structure: Verb (ない form) + ものでもない
explain: Means "I might do it, depending on the situation." It is an indirect, slightly reluctant yes. ないでもない is a similar, softer form.

examples.jp: {条件|じょうけん}によっては、{引|ひ}き{受|う}けないものでもない。
examples.en: Depending on the conditions, I might take it on.

examples.jp: {急|いそ}げば、{間|ま}に{合|あ}わないものでもない。
examples.en: If we hurry, we might make it.

examples.jp: {頼|たの}まれれば、{手伝|てつだ}わないものでもない。
examples.en: If asked, I might help.

quiz.q: {給料|きゅうりょう}が{上|あ}がるなら、{転勤|てんきん}し＿＿。
quiz.en: If my salary goes up, I might accept the transfer.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}が{謝|あやま}るなら、{許|ゆる}さ＿＿。
quiz.en: If he apologizes, I might forgive him.

quiz.q: {今|いま}から{始|はじ}めれば、{完成|かんせい}し＿＿が、{厳|きび}しいだろう。
quiz.en: If we start now, we might finish it, but it'll be tough.

structure: Verb (ない form minus ない) + ずじまい  (する → せずじまい)
explain: You wanted to do something, but in the end you never did it and now it's too late. It shows regret. Compare ないで{終|お}わる, which is plainer.

examples.jp: {忙|いそが}しくて、{旅行|りょこう}には{行|い}かずじまいだった。
examples.en: I was busy, so I never ended up going on the trip.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}の{名前|なまえ}は{聞|き}かずじまいだった。
examples.en: I never got to ask her name.

examples.jp: {買|か}った{本|ほん}を{読|よ}まずじまいで{捨|す}ててしまった。
examples.en: I threw away the book I bought without ever reading it.

quiz.q: {日本|にほん}にいる{間|あいだ}に{富士山|ふじさん}に{登|のぼ}りたかったが、{登|のぼ}ら＿＿だった。
quiz.en: I wanted to climb Mt. Fuji while in Japan, but I never did.

quiz.q: {結局|けっきょく}、{本当|ほんとう}の{理由|りゆう}は{分|わ}から＿＿だった。
quiz.en: In the end, I never found out the real reason.

quiz.q: お{礼|れい}を{言|い}おうと{思|おも}っていたのに、{言|い}わ＿＿になってしまった。
quiz.en: I meant to thank her, but I never did.

structure: Verb (ない form minus ない) + んばかりに / んばかりの + Noun  (する → せんばかり)
explain: Means something looks so strong that it seems about to happen, though it doesn't really. Used for strong feelings or states, like {泣|な}かんばかり. Compare とばかりに, which is about attitude, as if saying something.

examples.jp: {彼女|かのじょ}は{泣|な}き{出|だ}さんばかりの{顔|かお}をしていた。
examples.en: She looked as if she was about to cry.

examples.jp: {会場|かいじょう}は{割|わ}れんばかりの{拍手|はくしゅ}に{包|つつ}まれた。
examples.en: The hall was filled with thunderous applause.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は{飛|と}び{上|あ}がらんばかりに{喜|よろこ}んだ。
examples.en: He was so happy he almost jumped.

quiz.q: {犬|いぬ}はしっぽがちぎれ＿＿に{振|ふ}っていた。
quiz.en: The dog was wagging its tail so hard it looked like it would fall off.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は{今|いま}にも{殴|なぐ}りかから＿＿{勢|いきお}いで{怒|おこ}った。
quiz.en: He got angry as if he was about to hit someone.

quiz.q: {母|はは}は{私|わたし}の{合格|ごうかく}を{聞|き}いて、{踊|おど}り{出|だ}さ＿＿に{喜|よろこ}んだ。
quiz.en: My mother was so happy at my passing that she nearly started dancing.

structure: plain form / phrase + とばかりに
explain: Someone doesn't say it out loud, but their action clearly shows they mean it. Compare んばかり, which describes a state that seems about to happen.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}は「{出|で}ていけ」とばかりにドアを{開|あ}けた。
examples.en: He opened the door as if to say "Get out."

examples.jp: {子供|こども}は「{待|ま}ってました」とばかりにケーキに{手|て}を{伸|の}ばした。
examples.en: The child reached for the cake as if to say "Finally!"

examples.jp: {店員|てんいん}は{早|はや}く{帰|かえ}れとばかりに{片付|かたづ}けを{始|はじ}めた。
examples.en: The staff started cleaning up as if telling us to leave.

quiz.q: {彼女|かのじょ}は「もう{知|し}らない」＿＿{横|よこ}を{向|む}いた。
quiz.en: She turned away as if to say "I don't care anymore."

quiz.q: チャンス＿＿、{彼|かれ}は{一気|いっき}に{攻|せ}めた。
quiz.en: As if it were his chance, he attacked all at once.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}は「{当然|とうぜん}だ」＿＿{胸|むね}を{張|は}った。
quiz.en: He puffed out his chest as if to say "Of course."

meaning: extremely ~ / so ~ you can't describe it
structure: Noun / い-Adj (dictionary) + といったらない / ったらない
explain: Means a feeling or state is so strong it can't be put into words. It can be positive or negative. ったらない is the casual form.

examples.jp: {試験|しけん}に{合格|ごうかく}した{時|とき}のうれしさといったらなかった。
examples.en: I can't describe how happy I was when I passed the exam.

examples.jp: {満員|まんいん}{電車|でんしゃ}の{苦|くる}しさといったらない。
examples.en: Packed trains are unbearably uncomfortable.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}の{部屋|へや}の{汚|きたな}さったらない。
examples.en: His room is incredibly dirty.

quiz.q: {初|はじ}めて{見|み}た{富士山|ふじさん}の{美|うつく}しさ＿＿。
quiz.en: Words can't describe the beauty of Mt. Fuji when I first saw it.

quiz.q: {一人|ひとり}で{過|す}ごす{夜|よる}の{寂|さび}しさ＿＿。
quiz.en: Nights spent alone are unbearably lonely.

quiz.q: スピーチで{名前|なまえ}を{間違|まちが}えた{時|とき}の{恥|は}ずかしさ＿＿。
quiz.en: I can't describe how embarrassed I was when I got the name wrong in my speech.

structure: な-Adj stem + {極|きわ}まりない / {極|きわ}まる
explain: Means "extremely," usually for negative states like {失礼|しつれい} or {危険|きけん}. It is formal and strong. Both forms have the same meaning.

examples.jp: {彼|かれ}の{態度|たいど}は{失礼|しつれい}{極|きわ}まりない。
examples.en: His attitude is extremely rude.

examples.jp: {夜道|よみち}を{一人|ひとり}で{歩|ある}くのは{危険|きけん}{極|きわ}まりない。
examples.en: Walking alone at night is extremely dangerous.

examples.jp: {退屈|たいくつ}{極|きわ}まる{会議|かいぎ}だった。
examples.en: It was an extremely boring meeting.

quiz.q: {運転中|うんてんちゅう}にスマホを{見|み}るなんて、{危険|きけん}＿＿。
quiz.en: Looking at your phone while driving is extremely dangerous.

quiz.q: {約束|やくそく}の{時間|じかん}に{連絡|れんらく}もなく{来|こ}ないとは、{非常識|ひじょうしき}＿＿。
quiz.en: Not showing up or calling at the promised time is extremely thoughtless.

quiz.q: {彼|かれ}の{説明|せつめい}は{不親切|ふしんせつ}＿＿ものだった。
quiz.en: His explanation was extremely unhelpful.

structure: Noun + の{至|いた}り
explain: Means the highest degree of a feeling. It is very formal and often used in speeches, like {光栄|こうえい}の{至|いた}り. {若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}り means "a mistake of youth."

examples.jp: このような{賞|しょう}をいただき、{光栄|こうえい}の{至|いた}りです。
examples.en: It is a great honor to receive such an award.

examples.jp: {皆様|みなさま}にお{会|あ}いでき、{感激|かんげき}の{至|いた}りです。
examples.en: I am deeply moved to meet you all.

examples.jp: あれは{若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}りだった。
examples.en: That was a youthful mistake.

quiz.q: {先生|せんせい}にお{褒|ほ}めいただき、{恐縮|きょうしゅく}＿＿です。
quiz.en: I am truly humbled by your praise.

quiz.q: {大切|たいせつ}な{会議|かいぎ}に{遅|おく}れるとは、{不徳|ふとく}＿＿です。
quiz.en: Being late for an important meeting is entirely my fault.

quiz.q: {世界的|せかいてき}な{方|かた}とご{一緒|いっしょ}でき、{光栄|こうえい}＿＿です。
quiz.en: It is a great honor to be with someone so world-famous.

structure: Noun + の{極|きわ}み
explain: Means the highest point of something, often a feeling or a state. It is formal. Common phrases are {贅沢|ぜいたく}の{極|きわ}み, {疲労|ひろう}の{極|きわ}み, and {痛恨|つうこん}の{極|きわ}み.

examples.jp: {海|うみ}を{見|み}ながら{温泉|おんせん}に{入|はい}るのは{贅沢|ぜいたく}の{極|きわ}みだ。
examples.en: Soaking in a hot spring while looking at the sea is the height of luxury.

examples.jp: {徹夜|てつや}が{続|つづ}いて{疲労|ひろう}の{極|きわ}みに{達|たっ}した。
examples.en: After many all-nighters, I reached total exhaustion.

examples.jp: {決勝|けっしょう}で{負|ま}けたのは{痛恨|つうこん}の{極|きわ}みだ。
examples.en: Losing in the final is deeply painful.

quiz.q: このような{事態|じたい}を{招|まね}き、{遺憾|いかん}＿＿です。
quiz.en: We deeply regret causing this situation.

quiz.q: {高級|こうきゅう}ホテルのスイートに{泊|と}まるなんて、{贅沢|ぜいたく}＿＿だ。
quiz.en: Staying in a suite at a luxury hotel is the height of luxury.

quiz.q: {三日|みっか}{寝|ね}ずに{働|はたら}いて、{疲労|ひろう}＿＿に{達|たっ}した。
quiz.en: After working three days without sleep, I reached total exhaustion.

meaning: if ~, that's the end of it
structure: Verb (ば form) + それまでだ
explain: Means "if this happens, everything is over and it was all for nothing." It is often used for warnings. Compare までだ, which shows a calm decision.

examples.jp: どんなに{頑張|がんば}っても、{試験|しけん}に{落|お}ちればそれまでだ。
examples.en: No matter how hard you try, if you fail the exam, that's it.

examples.jp: {高|たか}いカメラも、{落|お}として{壊|こわ}せばそれまでだ。
examples.en: Even an expensive camera is useless if you drop and break it.

examples.jp: {才能|さいのう}があっても、{努力|どりょく}しなければそれまでだ。
examples.en: Even with talent, if you don't make an effort, that's the end of it.

quiz.q: {貯金|ちょきん}しても、{病気|びょうき}になれ＿＿。
quiz.en: Even with savings, if you get sick, it's all over.

quiz.q: {計画|けいかく}がよくても、{実行|じっこう}しなけれ＿＿。
quiz.en: Even a good plan is worthless if you don't carry it out.

quiz.q: データも、バックアップがなく{消|き}えてしまえ＿＿。
quiz.en: If data vanishes with no backup, that's the end of it.
